What movies do you like but everybody hates, and why? When The Matrix came out, every nerdy boy over 12 sang its praises. Every nerdy boy except me. I liked it (kinda) but I just couldn’t see the big deal about it. The action was good and everyone raved about the whole bullet time camera innovation. The soundtrack was phenomenal and the story and the main characters were intriguing. But I just couldn’t see the big deal. I just thought it was too silly for the movie to try to be deep and philosophical with its sociological commentary and high-brow sci-fi concepts, while at the same time engage in low-brow kung-fu action, psudo-BDSM rave culture, dystopian cyberpunk futurism, all the while having villains that looked like constipated insurance salesmen. I felt like the movie tried to be several things at once and took itself too seriously. I also felt that the movie would’ve been more enjoyable if it accepted how silly its concept was and focus more on its action scenes rather than having practically ever character besides Neo drifting off into some rambling philosophical stoner rant. Whenever I shared these criticisms with my nerd friends, they would turn red as though I demonstrated the most shocking of blasphemies. ‘You don’t get it. The Matrix is too deep for you to understand. Go watch your cartoons.’ That would be their usual response, but years would pass and my assessment would remain the same. THEN CAME THE MATRIX RELOADED I sat and watched it on TV long after its cinema premier. I wasn’t expecting much; some more philosophical sci-fi mumbo jumbo and a few over-rehearsed fight scenes. However, thirty minutes within the film I was finding myself thoroughly entertained. The movie went in the exact direction I wanted the first one to go. From the beginning to end the movie was a feast of God-like explosive superpowers, vast weaponry utilized in slow motion, explosions and swords slicing through speeding vehicles that contain time and space altering kung-fu fighting white rastas who can’t die, even in explosions. The movie relished in its stupidity and made no attempt to continue with the existential brouhaha of the original film. As an acne-riddled 18yo I ate it up like hot chicken soup but practically everyone I knew who worshipped the original, hated Reloaded with a passion. However, as admittedly dumb as it is, I consider it the superior movie. I haven't seen Resurrections yet but seeing that practically everyone loathes it I wouldn't be surprised if it turns out to be the best of the four.

Which kind of news do you like to access? Why? Anything that is relevant to my way of life and personal interests. It sounds selfish but it's the truth. In the school where I work I teach children the art of how to read the newspaper. Random citizen over 40: 'How to read the newspaper?!’ What?! Children must get in the habit of reading the entire newspaper……every day……front to back…..all the time. Otherwise they will be ignorant.’ To that idealistic but naive person I would reply no. The paradox of modern life is that the more time we spend viewing the news, the more uncritical we allow ourselves get henceforth the more dumb we get. If I lived my life according to the news today I'd think that: Growing up in Trinidad we are taught to listen to the news, not follow it. Because of our colonial past as a tiny island with a large grapevine network, we have had defiance and skepticism over the higher order injected into our bloodstream. ‘Massa say it against the law to trespass into his hunting ground…’ ‘Massa say all trespassers will be shot…' ‘Pahgo say that Massa gone with he family to live in Scotland. Don't even care about hunting ground....does come back to estate only once a year…' ‘I going into the hunting ground…’ Regardless of the critical thinking aspect, I tell students the worst thing to do a newspaper is read it from the front page to the back. It's just such a waste of time to read the newspaper/listen to the news programs in its entirety. The average Trinidadian newspaper usually has 100 pages more or less. 50% is usually advertisements. 20% is usually feature sections of mild interest i.e. How Edward overcame his disability to become a firefighter etc etc. 5% is sport 10% is specialized news: business, technology, health etc 5% is opinions and editorials 10% is relevant news that can be related to the average person. Of that 10% relevant Average Joe news only the first paragraph is of interest and more likely than not political slants are applied, data is exaggerated/underrepresented, status quo agendas and biases are applied to such and such. I tell students to spend more time skimming and skipping articles than actually reading the paper. Trinidad is a small country and we have the benefit of getting together in small units and discussing what we heard/saw on the news and filtering what may be truth from what is bulls**t based on our own common sense, trusted sources, scuttlebutt and that beautiful grapevine that we have that has never failed us for centuries. And the beauty of our grapevine style of news is that it doesn't cost a dime in subscription. Just go out into your world and be friendly. You'd pick up on some news relavent to your existence in less than an hour. Just be sure to verify your information with various trusted sources. All hail scuttlebutt. All hail the grapevine.

What is the most offensive thing you've been told while out on a date? A decade ago, I went on a date with someone I met on a dating website. I considered myself witty back then and a good few of my jokes had a sarcastic element to them. I met someone on the dating site who seemed to greatly appreciate deadpan quirkiness and sarcasm. She seemed to appreciate it a bit too much than is healthy for the average human. We arranged to meet at the mall. When we saw each other her eyes flitted away from mine and she stared at my shoes. 'That's the shoes you came to see me in?’ She then gave a soft yet caustic 'huh huh huh’ laugh to herself and began what would be a series of rolling eyes at everything that was said. I didn't understand what she meant. The shoes were almost new and were my best pair of sneakers. In fact, compared to her I was overdressed as she wore a rather unflattering suspender-skirt combo and an old pair of sandals. Minus the afro she looked a lot like the photo below but far more unkempt. I decided to ignore the comment. I asked her if she wanted to see a movie and she immediately made this whistling noise and started to go off about mindless dribble that Hollywood dishes out. I sort of agreed with her but at the same time her anti-Hollywood rant came across a bit on the pretentious side. We basically walked around the mall, her making random sarcastic comments about anything in her field of vision and me trying to agree with what she said and keep the conversation flowing. When we parted ways and I went homewards I did a quick mental audit of the date and my conclusion was that she definitely was not my cup of tea. However I told myself that maybe she probably suffers from some sort of anxiety and that's why she behaved so strangely. Maybe I ought to give her a chance. I called to tell her that I enjoyed our time and to find out if she was back home safe. 'Calling to see if I'm home safe?’ she replied, 'Bro. That's so corny. That's like men from the 50s.’ I could hear her faint 'huh huh huh’ laugh and could envision her rolling her eyes. I couldn't help but notice a strong pang of irritation develop within me. I put that aside and we spoke for a bit and ended up agreeing to meet her after she finished her classes the following day (she did a Degree in Computer Science). I told myself that with a little patience she would drop that caustic quirkiness of hers and start showing more warmth . I bought a rose for her and travelled to her school. I told myself what girl wouldn't love a man greeting her outside her class, well dressed and holding a rose for all her peers to see. Being that her class was due to over in a few minutes I basically ran up the street. When I arrived at the school, I called her phone to no avail. I told myself that her class was probably still in session. Then I saw a bunch of students filing out and I knew that she had to be among them. I saw her at the back, looking particular slovenly staring at me with her usual vacant stare. 'Oh my God.’ I saw her mouth the words as I moved towards her with the rose. However she mouthed it in distaste as though I were brandishing a slimy toad. As I reached within earshot she said the single most offensive thing I've ever heard someone mutter to me during a date. 'I was hoping you didn't come.’ This was followed by her 'huh huh huh’ laugh and rolling eyes. The irritation from the day before changed to anger. I tried to put aside the statement as another of her offbeat quirkiness and told her passionately about my hasty journey to get to her and how I ran up the street so as not to have her waiting. 'Dude,' she replied, 'That's psycho talk. Shut up.’ I paused and looked at her for a long while. Her supposed sense of humour was truly starting to rub me the wrong way. It sounded like a joke but came across like a vent fashioned into a rude and unfunny joke. She then talked about how she saw phone calls but intentionally disregarded them in the hopes that I would go away. She then mentioned that she saw me running up the street like a madman with a rose in my hand and felt so embarrassed. I remained silent. It was now a code red. Either I give her a piece of my mind or bow gracefully and leave. I opted for the latter and waited for a good civil moment to depart. 'You look like the type who doesn't go anywhere,' she continued, 'Seeing how you just ran through the streets just to see me from class you probably don't go out much. My ex boyfriend was a DJ. I used to get in to all the parties for free. He wasnt much to look at but a little sex now and again and I got into all the exclusive parties…..even aboard yachts. You know what a yacht is right?’ I remained silent. 'Dunno why I'm telling you all this………Look at you.You look like you want knock my head off don't you. Huh huh huh.’ It then dawned upon me that this girl was a twisted individual. This wasnt some quirky sense of humour. This was someone who got their kicks off of provoking others. Whatever hurt she experienced from those she loved in the past, she clearly wanted to exact that hurt on innocent people around her. When she arrived at her taxi stand I stood and waited in silence until she got into one. 'Well look at you,' she said in a last desperate attempt for a reaction from me, 'My knight in shining armour... You should maybe think about buying a car……it's kinda lame that…' The taxi driver sped off without waiting for her to finish what she was saying, probably cognizant that she was someone full of shit. I went home proud of myself that I didn't give her the reaction she desired. I deleted my account on the dating site. After that encounter I became far more conservative towards the use of sarcasm in humour and communication. I've been attracting much more likable and attractive females ever since that minor adjustment. So everything truly is a learning experience.

What television shows started strong only to become unwatchable later? Skins (2007 - 2013) The show was highly popular with millennials as it strove to give a realistic depiction of teenaged adults of that generation. The show, with its graphic portrayal of promiscuous sex and drug use among the majority of its main cast made it controversial at the time. Themes such as anorexia, poverty, depression, trauma, dysfunctional parenting etc were also touched on without succumbing to preaching or caricature. In essence the show was a comedy that subtly touched on some of the drama that went on in the personal lives of each of its characters. Generation 1 Without a doubt the first generation of Skins (Series 1 -2) is the true representation of the show. The first two seasons chronicles the lives of the above 9 teenagers. I enjoyed how no one was treated as the star of the show. Everyone had their positive traits as well as deep seated flaws but no one is given more screen time over the other or made into a token. The show focused on the youths as a group rather than as an hierarchy. The lifestyle may have been a tad exaggerated in its insistence that every character supposedly engaged in promiscuous sex and/or drug use. Besides that the show was an honest representation of teenaged millennials, written by an actual millennial, Jamie Brittain, who was 22 at the premier of the first season. The show launched the careers of actors Nicholas Hoult and Dev Patel who portrayed Tony and Anwar respectively. Generation 2 The second generation of Skins (Series 3–4) saw some changes. The comedic tone was increased as well as the amount of sex. The third season started off with an air of superficiality compared to the first generation but had a few well written moments and thoughtful episodes, particularly that of the trials and tribulations of teenaged Congolese immigrant Thomas. However the cast seemed all over the place and without developed characterization except that of cheap stereotypes (bully, geek, skater boy, drama queen, femme fatale etc.) Unlike Generation 1, this generation seemed to have an hierarchy among the cast as everything seemed to revolve around the characters Effy and Cook, who were, unsurprisingly, the most promiscuous and morally unscrupulous of the lot. Nearing the end of series 3 the show's writing started to wear thin. Shocks, drama and comedy were shoehorned in at every chance available. The show and its characters started losing their sense of direction and some of the themes that made them compelling characters in the beginning were abandoned in favour of sex and silliness. Some episodes were so ludicrous it became an effort to keep my eyes on the screen. The show seemed like a poor man’s imitation of itself. (So he's stealing a boat now…?) By series 4 it became painful to watch and I gave up. I have no intention to watch the third generation nor the American MTV remake. However the first generation of Skins remains a classic in my mind and a damned brilliant character study. It's hard for any writer to keep such a momentum going so you got to give the creators of the show credit for trying, even if they tried too hard in the end.

What is a show or movie which was super hyped up but ended up being terrible? The Underground (2006) Who doesn't love the Wayans? It seemed like they could do nothing wrong throughout the 80s, 90s and 00s. Keenen Ivory created In Living Color and directed the cult classic I'm Gonna Git You Sucka (1988) as well as the first two Scary Movies and White Chicks (2004). At one point in time he was the highest earning black film director in history. Shawn and Marlon had a large following with The Wayans Brothers television sitcom and a variety of acting credits in the Scary Movie films and In Living Color. Damon on the other hand……..Damon tries. He had a short unmemorable stint in Saturday Night Live where he played characters that would be deemed offensive by today's standards. He starred in a couple of duds throughout the 90s such as Blankman and Major Payne. He had a varying success with a few sitcoms under his belt but in 2006 he delivered the biggest turkey of his career with the Showtime sketch comedy show The Underground. Hyping it as 'In Living Color on steroids' the show was a truly tasteless and desperately unfunny attempt to zone in on the post-Chappelle Show audience. Some of the sketches include an ex-convict seducing and having sex with a very old woman, a talking vagina, and Peter Pan wanting to play with starving Somalians. Abandoning the witty and insightful parody of his brother Keenen, Damon opts for trashy and tasteless. Despite his sad attempts to gain attention by supposed shocking and edgy humour, no one raised an eyebrow and the show was cancelled without a murmur.

What food goes from delicious to revolting when you eat large amounts? Many moons ago…. I was hanging out with some friends after work in a bar, shooting some pool, enjoying a few rounds of drinks. It was customary (and proper etiquette) that the person who didn't buy any rounds go out and get some food for everyone. I would always volunteer to be the guy to get food. This is a bit embarrassing for me to admit but I secretly calculated that it was far cheaper to buy the food than a round of drinks for 7 — 10 people ( especially when ladies, requested premium stuff like mud slides and screwdrivers). A donut franchise had recently opened and it was just a few buildings away. A large box of donuts would've cost me almost half of what I usually paid for food. Plus there was less hassle, everything together in one neat box that weighed less than my arms. I ordered two dozen random donuts and returned to the bar, my beer waiting for me. Everyone cheered my idea for donuts. Beer and donuts….like Homer Simpson. We were gonna have a good time. No we weren't. After the first donut a few of us started feeling a bit queasy. We blamed it on the alcohol. It's when we attempted to eat the second donut was when disaster struck. As scrumptious and fresh as they were, they became absolutely revolting the second time around. I have a weakness for Long Johns but after wolfing one down, the second one I had my eye on looked like an instrument of torture. The donuts seemed to have brought in a premature hangover for the majority of us. One of the girls had to go to the toilet and was missing for a half hour. One of the fellas had to go throw up. There were still more than a dozen donuts remaining but I would've loved nothing more than to fling them into a dumpster. Only one guy had a hardcore stomach and survived the ordeal, consuming 3 while casually sipping on his beer. He offered to take the donuts home. Suddenly I became unpopular. They let me know that they were all aware that I chose to get food because it was cheaper for me. They really drilled it into me for taking my cheapness too far. Nothing feels worse than to be publicly humiliated by friends while suffering a sickly sweet, beer-donut hangover. I learned two lessons that day.

Are straight men ever attracted to very feminine gay guys? I saw one of the most beautiful girls I ever saw working behind the counter at a University campus KFC. She had bright hazel eyes that lay upon a soft, small face; an innocently seductive countenance that was accentuated with a small yet stately nose that anchored a teasing mouth. She nonchalantly chewed on gum as she stared at me with a defiant gaze. Her narrow shoulders wanted the protection of a man of resolve, a clever yet ruthless man; a man like me. Her hips swished and swayed as she trotted about in a fitted black trousers that revealed her shapely legs. I felt nervous as she stared at me, eyebrows lifted, awaiting for me to say something. Her breasts……….her breasts were……………..OK she was a bit on the flat side but that face alone was enough to build a Trojan horse for. She looked so cocky. I wanted to show her how cocky I was. I was going to say something like: ‘I order you to give me your number.’ What?? That’s real psycho-rapist stuff. How about: ‘A two piece with you on the side.’ Yeah. That’s class. Ok. Say it………….no. That’s stupid. I’ll just give my order. But I’ll say it seductively. ‘Can I take your order?’ Who said that!? That voice? That tinny, cloying but clearly masculine voice; the voice of an old, curmudgeonous geezer. It felt as though the circuits in my brain sparked and scrambled. It felt as though there was a glitch in the matrix; a tear in the fabric of our universe. It made me shudder and feel paranoid. ‘Sir. Can I take your order please?’ That awful old man voice. It came from the beautiful girl in front of me. I looked at her name tag. ‘Hello. My name is Aaron.’ The most beautiful KFC maiden was a man. An emotion never experienced before; an amalgamation of revulsion, curiosity and betrayed lust made me feel like running away but keeping my eyes on her/him while running. It felt almost similar to the feeling one gets to suddenly detecting that you're being watched and scrutinized by a hidden figure; a feeling of vulnerability. I had to leave the KFC to process what the hell just happened. Did I question my sexuality? Damn right I did. I came to the verdict that I wasn’t gay but by instinct, I was wired to be attracted to feminine features. I learned that, if possible, always read someone’s name tag before you decide to lust after them.

What are some of the biggest casting blunders in Hollywood movies? I know I may be in the minority with this opinion but when I saw that this guy would be cast as Peter Parker in the first major studio Spiderman movie, disappointment is not strong enough of a word to describe how I felt. Tobey Maguire does not have the wit, charisma and charm of a traditional Peter Parker. Not only that, Maguire was too old for the role from the very first movie. When I saw 27 year old Maguire walking about high school with a jacket, book bag and a distinct 5 o’clock shadow on his face I was immediately taken out of the movie. (Yeah that's definitely a teenaged schoolboy boarding a bus and not a smirking, semi-creepy man pushing 30) Peter Parker is a charming and witty young man, loyal to friends and family, a great problem solver and a smartass with a touch of geekiness. The only characteristic Tobey Maguire demonstrated from the above was the geekiness, of which he laid on as thick as cheesecake. Maguire’s Spiderman was this awkward, pitiable schmuck who had as much charisma and charm as a mild-mannered peeping tom. The whole shtick the producers seemed to go with was to make Peter Parker nothing but a sad, bullied nerd because I guess maybe they arrogantly believed Spiderman fans are nothing but a bunch of nerds who love the comic book not because of its quality story and characters but because it supports a geek fantasy of getting fantastic superpowers through simple means, getting to beat up thugs and bullies and winning chicks. Sam Raimi’s Spiderman targeted that niche when they gave us the whimpering, sensitive, thin-lipped Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker in my honest opinion. Maybe that's my personal opinion but personality aside, Maguire doesn't even have the physical attributes. Spiderman/Parker is 5′10, late teens-early 20s, lean, long-limbed, sinewy and with a head of thick brunette hair. He basically has to have the physique of a well experienced trapeze artist due to all the climbing and swinging Spiderman does. At his best in the film Tobey Maguire was a short limbed and somewhat stocky man measuring somewhere between 5′7 and 5′8 with a crop of thin hair above his smirking, punchable face. I grew up watching Spiderman cartoons and gaining a familiarity with Parker's smart, resonating and confident tone. Maguire's whiny, eerily pubescent voice gave a measure of cringe and creepiness. I am not a fan of Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker and will hold that view for the rest of my life. Andrew Garfield and Tom Holland may not be the gold standard either but they are a lot more closer to the mark. Here's hoping that they get it right the next movie.

Which is the most misunderstood film of all time? It shocks me to this day that people think Breakfast at Tiffany’s (1961) is a charming, feelgood rom-com. Even though the screenplay was sugar coated to heck, the source material is actually a character study of grooming, abuse and promiscuity and its impact on a young rural woman deliriously pretending to be something she isn’t. No one talks about the Truman Capote book because reading it is a sobering experience that takes away a lot of the shimmer from the hugely popular movie. Holly Golightly is a really messed up, poverty stricken girl from Texas with the birth name of Lula Mae. She ran away from home to an older man through which she was groomed and became his wife at the age of 14. She then ran away from him to New York under a false identity. Through manipulation, fraud and mafia related espionage she maintains a high end Brownstone apartment above her means. She courts several wealthy suitors by throwing lavish parties and intends to marry the richest of the lot. In the film and the book she shows symptoms of borderline personality and disassociative identity disorder. When things don't go her way financially she goes further into her fantasy of being a high society socialite by simply walking around in her best clothes and pretending to shop/hang out at Tiffany's or other famous luxury stores and locations . Audrey Hepburn is cute and charming. Holly Golightly is not. She is a warped individual that is prone to fits of anger, delusion and self destruction. She is pretentious and borderline narcissistic with the only ease of conscious being her flimsy belief that she will help her abject brother at some point in time. This delusion does not work out well for her. If the film had ended the way the novella ended it would have been a tragic, small town, wide eyed kid comes to New York in search of the American dream drama very much in the vein of the not so feelgood Midnight Cowboy (1969). The final scene with Holly and Paul finding her cat (named Cat) in the alley in the pouring rain is supposedly where the moral of the story comes in. It is the part of the film that transforms it from a softened character study into a full blown romantic comedy. It gives a moral that love can heal all as both Paul and Holly acknowledge their faults, subtly agree to change their ways and direct their love to one another. I have ambiguous feelings towards the ending but it is admittedly cute. However, I think any licensed psychologist would agree that Holly Golightly from the film Breakfast at Tiffany's is a movie that is a somber study of the neuroses and disorders a young female runaway from a broken home has to endure disguised as a sophisticated rom-com. Edit: Several commenters have been stating that they don't see why I refer to this as a misunderstood movie, that it deviated from the novel but as a film it is not misunderstood. Yes it is a misunderstood movie. Many people believe it is a simple love story about two good looking, fashionable young people falling in love in New York to the tune of Moon River. Generations of people believed that Holly Golightly was classy, an inspiration and an icon in lifestyle and fashion. Many girls of the era grew up wanting to be just like Holly Golightly without thoroughly understanding that she was a deeply flawed character with deep seated personality disorders. If this is not a misunderstood movie then the word misunderstood is ‘misunderstood.’

I'm a school custodian and when people ask me what's my job I'm ashamed to tell them. What's the best way I could say what I do without saying I'm a custodian? Embrace the fact that you are a janitor. Yes. I said it. A janitor. You work for a living. You work hard. You are valuable salt of the Earth. People feel comfortable around you and feel more at ease to talk to you because you hold no airs about yourself. People admire you because you do a job that most people don't want and when you do it with pride you are an inspiration. I'm sure if you tell the staff around you your plans to get a degree or invest in a small business you will get an overwhelming amount of support. Everyone loves to see the little guy make small steps. No one likes to hear the big rich CEO gushing about a planned merger or a thriving stock portfolio. No. People love to hear about the janitor who saved his money and started his own cleaning company. You also have the benefit of always knowing who are your real friends. Lawyers, doctors and politicians don't have that benefit. Everyone is running to kiss their ass and use them. Nobody is running to kiss Larry the janitor’s ass and use him. You know that people who don't respect you or your work, no matter how well you perform it, are people to stay away from. You don't have to have your back against the wall to see your enemies. Be proud of who you are. You work hard. Not many people do that. And if anyone asks what you do for a living say with pride that you are a school janitor. Their reaction will say a lot about them Written by a former delivery ‘boy.’

What does a $1,500,000 house look like where you live? Like the house the average lower-middle class bloke lives in. In Trinidad house prices are notoriously inflated. Real estate agents will tell you it's all about supply and demand but in reality it is because there are no checks and balances to the real estate sector. The above image is of a house built and sold by a private developer. Nothing looks outstanding about it. Heck, the owner didn't even bother to take a good photo of the house when the grass develops nicely and in nice weather to show off its mustard paint job. This house looks like how most Government commissioned, detached, single family housing units look like. A 5000 sq ft, 2–3 bedroom cookie cutter nestled amongst a swarm of others like it as far as the eyes can see. It's not unlikely that the guys who built the privately sold house are the same ones awarded the contracts to build the Government properties. Conflict of interest? Maybe. Will the private developer extend a lot of effort to his private development which is monitored by public opinion, customer satisfaction and subject to legal recourse? Yes. Will the private developer extend the same effort to a big fat Government contract whereby he's unsupervised in the making of hundreds of matchbox style cookie cutters, can bribe public officials to cut corners and is shrouded from public opinion as all fault is levied towards 'the corrupt government?’ Not so much. In essence, $1.5 mil in TT dollars can get you a generic matchbox style house with a tiny piece of yard to plant some flowers/herbs. You can apply through the Government if you have chronic problems in regards to finances and all it takes is just bending over backwards to show political allegiance and screaming to the heavens how hard your life in a gross public display. You can do that or be put on a waiting list and expect to be responded to in at least 25–30 years. When you do get your $1.5 mil Government house don't be so quick to celebrate. Crime, shoddy infrastructure and utilities and poor environmental planning are rampant in Government housing projects. So maybe a privately developed $1.5 mil house is the better option? With the private housing developments, there has been a growth in unapproved or downright illegal developments by unscrupulous developers. The house in the very first photo could seem like a pretty decent option but bear in mind these three possibilities. So in conclusion, in Trinidad $1.5 million can allow you to pick your own poison when it comes to housing.

Are there parents who regret having mixed-race children? My paternal grandfather Anthony Roy Hughes was a white Grenadian and his wife Mona (paternal grandmother) was a mixed raced Grenadian. Together they had six children and enjoyed an upper middle class existence after they both migrated to Trinidad, him working for Shell Oil and her working as a French school teacher. They bought a large house together in a picturesque neighborhood called Cascade. Things were definitely not as happy as it appears in the above photos. Grandfather was abusive with untreated manic depression/bipolar symtoms. It was said by my family that he never truly loved my grandmother. His original goal was to find a white wife (as was the norm during colonial times) and she was the closest thing he could get towards that goal. It was also said that he gave preferable treatment to his more Caucasoid children and was particularly unloving to the others who weren't (my father [center of the above photo] being a prime target due to his being the darkest of the lot). In just a few years within the marriage he lost his job at Shell Oil as being seen as unfit. Despite being given a severance payout he depended on his wife's teaching salary to provide for him and the children. Jobless and prone to depressive episodes he would make every attempt to find merriment outside of his home and when he did come home his frustrations over his incapacities and failures were taken out on his wife and children. My aunt would tell me that they would hear him singing drunken songs as he came up the hill towards the house and according to what song he sang, they would know whether he was ready to give everyone a whupping or if he would go shut himself in his bedroom for several hours. They prayed that it would be the latter. He depended on his wife's salary and her kind nature to hold the family together, pay the bills and take care of the house. Meanwhile he repaid her kindness by being more physically and emotionally abusive. Grandma was stricken with motor neuron disease in her early 40s and wasted away wheelchair bound for the last years of her life, passing away at the relatively young age of 48. All this tragedy and abuse contributed to their children suffering from various neuroses and mental illnesses. Only two managed to have some measure of success in their personal lives while the rest succumbed to directionless lives of struggle and financial and mental hardships, the youngest committing suicide at age 40 and two recently passing away alone and in squalor. But rather than delve into personal history (and there's a lot), let me answer the original question. Are there parents who regret having mixed-raced children? It is possible that my grandfather regretted his mixed raced children and harbored deep prejudices. It is also possible that he loved his mixed race children but his untreated mental illness brought out the worst in him. The answer in regards to my grandfather is probably. He showed no remorse when his wife died, relieved himself of any further fatherly duties and made no attempt to establish communication with his children. He sold the house and remarried (his long sought after white bride) a few years after his first wife's death. He died a lonely divorcée in 1994. Would he have made a greater effort to be a better father if he had found his white bride and had a flock of children, all the same complexion as him? No one knows.

What should every foreigner know about your country in terms of food, tourist destinations, demography, best time to visit, and USP of your country? Trinidad is actually two islands, Trinidad and Tobago. Trinidad is the oil and gas island. Tobago is the tourist island. We have the only ‘pitch lake’ in the entire world. We invented the steel drum/pan. Yes we did. Look it up. Trinidad had the most thriving KFC in the world at one point in time. Also Trinidad has more KFCs per capita than any country in the world. 59 restaurants in an area smaller than Delaware (which has only 13). In many ways we are very similar to Brazil. We once possessed the world’s hottest pepper, the Moruga Scorpion (we still like to believe it’s the world’s hottest). We put ketchup, mustard and pepper sauce on EVERY fast food. Do not open a fast food restaurant here without having copious amounts of these available to the general public. Don’t even get us started on garlic sauce. If you hate rice you will not last a month here. We make some of the finest rums in the world. Yet beer is more widely consumed. Marijuana is sort of legal. Just don’t get caught selling it. We are very liberal yet quite conservative at the same time. We don’t frown that much upon prostitution, once you’re not a transvestite prostitute. Then you might be asking for trouble.

Which actor played a villain role too well for comfort? Ann Dowd as Joan in Hereditary. ***Spoiler Alert*** The performance by this relatively unknown actress blew me away and everyone who I've known to watch this film. Joan is the motherly figure who befriends Toni Collette's main character Annie who is going through a really tough time. Toni Collette's exemplary performance as a depressed middle aged mother suffering from tragedy is complimented by Ann Dowd's Joan who wins the heart of the viewers as a sympathetic, patient and caring matriarchal figure in the first half, only to suddenly transform into someone truly terrifying in the second half. What was scary for me about her performance was the genuine warmth she generated from the very moment she entered the screen. I can't see anyone being unable to put their guard down and love and accept this lady. It didn't seem like a performance at all. It seemed like that is how Ann Dowd really is. However when she lifts the veil it is almost bloodcurdling to see the transformation in her appearance and especially in her voice. Nothing is more scarier to me than evil people convincingly disguised as good and with that Ann Dowd truly delivered.

What has an employee said that immediately caused you to fire them? Jerome (not real name) was a new worker with a big mouth. He was 28 years old at the time, quite older than most of the guys he worked with like myself yet he acted, at best, like a spoilt 15 year old. He was always talking. He always had an opinion about something. He always had to question even the most simple orders and instructions. He believed himself to be the most intelligent person to ever walk the floor of the warehouse and always spoke at length of all the flaws he saw in our system and what he would do to fix the business if he were in charge. Our job was simple: a retail store wants products that we have, we go out with our grocery carts, pallet jacks, forklifts etc, get the products and have them packaged and ready for delivery in the morning. Not Jerome. Jerome's job was to distact you from what you were doing to talk shit about the company and how the money wasn't worth it. He would quote some nonexisting OSHA law that the company wasn't complying with and how he could sue the company if he wanted to. He would discuss his harebrained, get rich quick schemes that he never had to guts to actually attempt. He bragged about his family in the US waiting for him and how he didn't need to work himself like a slave for chump change like we did. At any given day he probably put out 20% of the output of the average worker. He was on a six month probationary period of which it would be decided whether he would be contracted as a permanent worker, given extended probation or let go. No one expected him to be permanently hired. Everyone basically tried to tolerate him for the six month probationary period as best as they could. However he started taking his shenanigans to the next level. He started making the (typically secluded) shampoos lane in the back warehouse his secret hideout. The lane was quiet, had no cameras and far away from our superiors’ field of vision. He decided to set up a makeshift man-cave behind a pallet of Tresemmé 2 in 1 Shampoo and Conditioner. There he would smoke, talk shit with the rare, harmless worker who came by for shampoos and he would watch rap music videos on his cell phone. At the month's end all warehouse workers were allowed to take from the damaged products. We had our own system of fairness whereby we rotated each worker to get a chance to get first pick among the damages. Jerome couldn't give a rat's ass about the system. During the third month of his employ it was observed that practically all of the best damaged goods had gone missing. A co-worker and myself smelt a rat in Jerome and we went to his man cave while he was on lunch and saw the damages were there hidden in boxes. We reported it to the supervisor who came and saw it. He held an emergency meeting and asked for the person who put those damaged goods in the back to come forward. Everyone eyed Jerome angrily but he remained silent. The supervisor reported the matter to the manager who reported it to the company owner and she immediately put a stop to the free damages giveaway. Now the anger towards Jerome had turned into a bloodlust. However the more angry everyone got the more lazy and defiant Jerome became. He was smart enough to abandon his man-cave after his attempted theft but he still spent more than half his working day loitering and talking shit. Every year the company paid for the company staff to have a party, usually at a classy sports bar or a nightclub. We all looked forward to it including Jerome who discussed at length his intention to get drunk off of free premium drinks and score with one of the pretty head office girls. However, one fateful afternoon the owner of the store had an impromptu meeting with everyone in the warehouse. She explained that the company decided to change the format of the staff party. She explained that it was expensive and inefficient having this party every year when too many employees ran up a bill drinking premium drinks all night and then not being able to come to work the following day. She gave the disappointing news that this time the party would be held at 12pm — 7pm the upcoming Sunday. Jerome released a snorting laugh while she spoke. Everyone in the warehouse went dead silent. No one had ever dared interrupt the owner, far less mock her. 'Excuse me,' she said, 'Is there something amusing?’ 'Nobody ever heard of a party 12 o clock in the afternoon,' Jerome said in his spoilt 15 year old voice. 'I've been to many parties 12 o clock in the afternoon' she replied. 'Yeah, birthday parties for kids' Jerome said smugly and looked about for someone to laugh but found only silence. The owner asked Jerome his name and how long he worked in the warehouse. Afterwards she continued her talk uninterrupted but after the meeting was dismissed she, the manager and Jerome went into an office for a talk. Some minutes later Jerome was seen leaving the compound, he was terminated from the job. Sad thing for Jerome was the owner apparently thought over what he said about the party and changed her mind about it. We were allowed to have our traditional, late into the night, party albeit minus the free premium drinks. We had a great time dancing the night away and toasting Jerome whose big mouth finally done some good for a change. Footnote 6/6/2023: There are a few commenters who seem to doubt the validity of my story on the grounds that 'so how come they didn't just fire Jerome as he's on probation?’ Probation is a process of testing and observing a new worker for short period. We signed a contract that we would be terminated on the grounds of serious offences like drug use, sexual harassment, assault, excessive absenteeism etc. Being a crappy worker and talking shit all day wouldn't get you terminated instantly but would definitely make you fail your probation and would have you under their radar for possible termination, which is exactly what happened in Jerome's case. Please. If you find all of this fantastic and unbelievable you are free to shake your head and scroll down.

Why would I kill a mugger in self-defense? Are my valuables worth more than their life? I’ve been mugged four times. Two of these muggings were violent. In these muggings I had my face punched relentlessly. I had a beer bottle smashed on my head, requiring stitches. I had a gun pointed at my face. I got my pants and underwear torn open and had to walk to the police station afterwards with my junk in my hands. In both muggings I got laughed at by the muggers. I’ll never forget the moment when one of the muggers looked at me sitting defeated on the curb, robbed, bleeding and beaten. I’ll never forget how in the silence that followed he looked me in the eyes and growled ‘That’s how it is.’ In that situation I’m certain that same mugger would’ve killed me if needed. I felt a deep cynical hatred in him; that beating me to a pulp satisfied some inner rage he compartmentalized towards society. No. It wasn’t just about the money for them. They felt the world owed them something that they themselves couldn’t fathom what. What is it that I had that was so valuable to these muggers? In total I lost around $300 TT (43US), a cheap cell phone and wallet with my identification cards which would’ve been no value to them. Someone who so callously and casually engages in theft while inflicting violence upon his victims is someone who has agreed that they do not value your life nor theirs. Why must I pay special consideration to their lives while being beaten senselessly or having a knife or gun pointed at me? Does the small amount of money lost bother me? No. What bothers me is the reality that there are some people out there who saw me like garbage and inflicted a hateful beating while threatening my life, knowing fully well that the loot probably wasn’t worth it. My valuables may not be worth more than a human life but if in self defense I had fatally shot my armed and/or violent mugger, I would not be sending flowers to his family nor showing up at his funeral, nor would I suffer any sleepless nights over it. As the old folks in Trinidad love to say; how you make your bed is how you lie on it.

What is the cringiest name you have seen/heard given to a child? I worked in a school where there was a girl named Supreme Hurst. I asked her how she ended up with such a unique name and she said she hadn’t the faintest clue other than it was the name her dad chose. Out of curiosity I looked up her name to see if there was some kind of meaning behind it. I found out that there is an Oldsmobile car model with that very name. I would’ve loved to have known if it was by coincidence or intentional that her dad named her after such an unimpressive car. When I showed her the car she was quite disappointed it wasn’t a luxury vehicle. She explained that once she got married her name would change so it didn’t bother her that much. Some months later she got into a relationship with a boy named Stark Grimes. I kid you not. He’s not an aspiring rapper. That’s the name on his birth certificate. I was flabbergasted. The girl with the weirdest name I ever heard of was dating the boy with the weirdest name I ever heard of. I told her in jest that if they got married Supreme Grimes seemed far worse than Supreme Hurst. Stark wasn’t a bad chap. He was witty, well behaved and had a YouTube channel that had some pretty well produced Trinidad-oriented comedy. However the relationship didn’t last. Supreme Hurst and Stark Grimes went their separate ways after a few months of dating. Unfortunately I can’t find any of Supreme’s social media profiles. It’s been a decade since I heard from her. I’m assuming she got married and had that long awaited name change. I just hope for her sake she didn’t get married to a guy with the surname Dick.

What annoys you about people your age? People my age (37) are in the middle aged category and tend to be very sensitive when discussing their career, life goals and personal lives. It may just be me but I’ve noticed that most people here in their mid 30’s - early 40s tend to be more private about themselves and their personal lives and they are a lot more risk averse. I’ve observed passive aggressiveness more common among people my age (35 - 44) than in any other age group. In my experience in workplace settings I’ve also noticed that brown-nosing, bad workaholic tendencies, exploitative/manipulative behavior, micromanaging etc comes more from people my age and rarely from those in young or older categories. My explanation for this is the possible desperation to achieve certain goals, by whatever means, as they think that ‘time is running out.’ I know everyone (including myself) exhibit some of these traits at some point in their life but for me it’s the reason I rarely become friendly with people around my age at work.

Have you ever dated anyone who was married? If so, how did the relationship go? My ex, the mother of my child, was still legally married when we started dating. She was still legally married when she got pregnant with our daughter and to this day she is still legally married to him after we've completely parted ways for almost two years. I am not one to go after married women but she claimed when I first met her that she was entering divorce proceedings. That, along with several other promises, was never fulfilled. The relationship was the textbook whirlwind romance. Things took off like lightning and then thunder crashed and a heavy rain fell on me for several years. My advice is to avoid dating anyone married but doesn't have the decency to follow through with a proper divorce yet wants to enter into the world of dating. They made a vow to their spouse to be with them for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health. If they don't have the decency to get a divorce, what makes you think they will be loyal to you? I guarantee they will make you worse, poorer and sick all at once.

Have you ever realized that you were wrong about someone? I once worked part-time transporting furniture for a small Mom n Pop furniture store. Everyone was wonderful. Mom used to cook us lunch every week. Pop used to carry us out fishing down the islands on weekends in his boat. The boys who did the heavy lifting/labour were very polite and friendly and we would go to each other’s house every Friday evening after having a couple of beers. There was a real camaraderie prevalent in the store that made everyone there feel like a 2nd family, an atmosphere far removed from the resentment and seething suspicion that reigned in my day job at a public office. One day, one of the boys, Chris, was excited because a former worker named Carlton was getting back his position at the store. Chris spoke in volumes about the greatness of Carlton; how Carlton was the funniest, most sharp and charismatic person he ever met. Carlton was also one of the best workers; helpful and diligent. He spoke how he missed Carlton so much, that Carlton was the like the life-essence of the store and such and such. I would be lying if I said that it didn’t make me a tad jealous to hear all this praise about some kid who worked here for a couple months and unceremoniously left, but nevertheless I was mystified by this Carlton persona. When he finally arrived, my expectations were so heightened that in my mind I envisioned the Ultimate Boy Scout entering the store flashing a 1000 Watt smile and making flora and fauna thrive around him with just his illuminating presence. Instead, this scruffy, pot-bellied unshaven man-child wearing the most slovenly and ill-fitting of clothing came into my vision. He was indeed sharp and witty but much like that of a snake-oil salesman or a streetwise con-man. He talked endlessly. It seemed as though his brain never needed a pit stop. He was always in the know or so he liked to make it seem. While sitting around outside waiting for customers, he would point out to me all the hustlers, the liars, high rollers, low riders, all the suckers, the strugglers, the ex-cons, the soon-to-be behind bars, the pipers (bums) and the sprangers (petty thieves), horner-men (men who get involved with married women) and panty-men (men who were beaten by their wives). Carlton knew everyone and everyone knew Carlton. He was loved by the general public and could easily hustle a cigarette or $5 from from practically any random person. Everyone in the store, in the entire street for that matter, was so happy to have him back. Everyone except me, that is. I thought he was nothing more than a glorified scoundrel. He was indeed charismatic and would rule the group conversations. He had a gift for ‘busting balls’ and would send a volley of golden stingers your direction without pause the minute you tried to mock him or make fun of his shabby appearance. However he loved attention, seemed to take everything for a joke and could never shut up. He knew that he irritated me but that didn’t bother him. With his skill and experience as a natural born hustler he never cared for what people thought of him. However it did bother him that I would choose Chris as a loader to go out on deliveries with rather than him. This was a sore point with him because I would share half my transport fee with Chris and it pained him to see Chris alone raking in all that money. However, one day Chris couldn’t make it to work and I had to carry Carlton with me as a loader. Carlton was overjoyed and already started planning what he was gonna do with ‘his half’ of the transport money. I thought it was rather bold of him to assume that because I paid Chris half, I would pay him half. I had specifically told that braggart Chris not to tell anyone how much I paid him so as to avoid situations like this. I immediately got upset. The item was one of our dreaded over sized wardrobes. These were notorious for transport because they were massive and ill-built from the cheapest materials. You had to strap them to your tray with expert precision because the slightest turbulence could make them rock and the cheap pitch pine would crack on itself. They were also very cumbersome to get through the customers’ doors as they were so wide and tall. The last one I transported to a rural area with really bad roads suffered a cracked mirror and a few broken dowels. I had to reimburse the customer for the damage. I groaned knowing that not only did I have to carry one of these monstrosities but I had to go with blabbermouth Carlton and in weather that appeared to be inclement. After hauling the massive wardrobe onto the van, covering it with a tarpaulin and strapping it to the best of our abilities we headed northwards towards the customer location. Carlton, a chain smoker, needed money borrowed to buy cigarettes. I loaned him some money and stopped so he could go and buy a pack at a nearby shop. Several minutes later he returns with but a single cigarette in his mouth. ‘Where’s the pack?’ I asked, wondering if he shafted me. ‘I forget I owe that shop money,’ he replied with a proud smile. I shook my head and sighed as I knew it would be a long evening. As we drove Carlton spoke of his lofty goals and plans. He wanted to open a casino. He wanted to operate a farm. He wanted to be a porn film director. He wanted to start his own political party and so on and so on. He asked to borrow some more money for a cigarette and I told him no. Unfazed he looked out the window for a while and asked me to stop the vehicle for a minute. I did so and watched as he approached a random stranger on the sidewalk and successfully talked his way into getting a cigarette. We then took off but after a few minutes the wind began to blow powerfully and rain started falling in torrents. I could hear the wind making the tarpaulin flap about like a living creature. I asked Carlton to check on the wardrobe for me. To see if it was getting wet anywhere. ‘You crazy,’ he cried, ‘In this rain? I strap down that tarpaulin. No way it getting wet.’ I insisted he go check but he refused on account of the heavy rain. In anger I went out back myself, hopped onto the tray and meticulously checked the wardrobe for any sign of rain infiltrating onto the wardrobe. There was none. Carlton was right. The tarpaulin was indeed strapped well. I returned soaked and watched Carlton as he laughed at me and was in the process of lighting a spliff. I asked him what the hell he thought he was doing. He told me that he found this weed in his backpocket. Today was his lucky day. I told him that I wasn’t going to jail for him and his weed. He laughed and said that we were deep in ‘the bush’ (countryside) and it was raining heavily. What would be the chances of police passing and even if they did, they wouldn’t care. He had a point but I didn’t like the idea of him getting so comfortable in my van. We reached our destination and saw that it was a large apartment complex. We called the customer and she informed us that her apartment was situated at the top floor. That meant that we had to haul this thing up a long flight of stairs and through a narrow balcony area with a low ceiling and then somehow get it through a tiny doorway. ‘Forget about it,’ Carlton said. ‘What?’ I replied. ‘That wardrobe cannot reach there.’ I looked at him as he seemed a bit high. In my mind it seemed he was being lazy. He then began to discuss the length and width of the wardrobe versus the width of the staircase, the corridor and the height of the door-frame. ‘That wardrobe will never get into that apartment. This was a waste-run.’ There was a seriousness in his voice I never heard before. I then began to understand where he was coming from. The thin staircase met the balcony-corridor at right angles, unless one of us could’ve walked on air, there was no way we could’ve gotten the wardrobe around the corner, let alone through the minuscule doorway. On the phone I explained this to the customer and she was beginning to acquiesce. Suddenly her boyfriend took the phone from her and started growling that he was coming to help us carry it inside. He hung up and then we saw this stocky, bald-headed and barechested ignoramus walking out the apartment and downstairs to our direction with a furious expression on his face. Carlton looked at me and said, ‘Boy, forget that man. Let’s just take down this wardrobe and drive off. That wardrobe cannot fit in that apartment. That man is an idiot.’ I felt bewildered. On the one hand I believed Carlton was right but on the other hand I didn’t want this journey to be a waste. Maybe there was some way in which that wardrobe could reach inside… ‘Boy, let’s go.’ Carlton continued, ‘We have to pay for this wardrobe if it falls off that balcony. Don’t study this ass. Let’s go.’ The man came up to the van and began rapping his knuckles against the window. He then gestured with his palms facing forward as if to say, ‘So what the f***?’ ‘Come let us carry this thing upstairs,’ the man demanded, ‘Is money I pay for this thing. Let’s go, let’s go.’ By him saying that I felt it my duty to haul the wardrobe up to his apartment. I had his $300 transport fee in my pocket. I was about to hop out the van and proceed with the haul when Carlton went out of the van and approached the man. Carlton tried to explain to the man the impossibility of getting a wardrobe of such dimensions into the apartment. That he should let us return it the store and choose something smaller. The man got offended by the latter statement and proceeded to verbally abuse us both. I then gathered the courage to tell the man that as transport agents we are not bound to deliver the item inside the home, that we fulfilled our duty by bringing it to the location. The man started getting aggressive and demanded that we take down his property off the van and give him back his $300 transport fee. I politely gave him his money and with Carlton we unstrapped the wardrobe and lay it next to him on the ground. We then watched as the man tried to find some men in the area to help him haul the wardrobe upstairs. ‘Let’s go,’ Carlton said, ‘That wardrobe will fall to pieces off that balcony in a few minutes time from now. Mark my words. Damn jackass…’ We left the man as we saw that he hired two men to help him carry the wardrobe up the stairs. We drove looking at him hand gesturing to his men his great plan on how to maneuver the wardrobe around the bend. While heading back I felt thankful that someone more streetwise, instinctive and assertive was with me, otherwise I would’ve been pushed around by that belligerent idiot and would've probably damaged/destroyed the wardrobe to my expense. Suddenly my phone rang. It was the boss. My heart froze. The boss would only call if we were in trouble. I answered the phone and the boss frantically asked what just happened. He said that the customer just called him and said that the wardrobe fell off the balcony and broke. That he wants to come in the morning to get it replaced for a smaller wardrobe. I explained what happened and to my surprise the boss laughed. ‘So you didn’t attempt to carry the wardrobe upstairs?’ ‘No.’ I replied, 'He hired his own people.’ ‘Thank God,’ he replied with a sigh, ‘You’re not supposed to carry any furniture up any stairs. That’s the customer’s responsibility. I explained that to them when they bought it. They can’t get any refund or exchange.’ I laughed to myself and explained the news to Carlton. Expecting at least a smile I was surprised to see an angry look on his face. He was upset that I gave the man back his $300 transport fee when I could’ve simply called the boss the whole time. Carlton sorely lamented the lost $150 that he was due that could’ve paid for lunch and cigarettes for the rest of the week. But all in all it was a fun and memorable evening and the beginning of a beautiful friendship. Carlton's charm grew on me from then on and I started to grow attached to his manic but quick-witted character. I felt bad that I labelled him as a glorified scoundrel and I’ve since learned never to be so quick to judge. Carlton (left) with a happy customer.

What single moment in a film was an example of some of the greatest acting you've ever seen from an individual or ensemble cast? The Last Picture Show (1971) is, in my honest opinion, the greatest piece of ensemble acting I've ever seen. I would go as far and say that this is one of the rare moments in cinema where a certain magic takes over and the movie takes unexplainable life of its own. It is one of the few movies that can move me to tears even if I were to watch it reading captions on mute. The acting, both vocal and non-vocal, is that good. But before I go on a rant, for those who don't know about the film, it revolves around various characters living in a dusty, dying small town in Texas. Life for practically everyone is uneventful and everyone shares a certain yearning; for the older generation it is of good times gone by and things that could've been, for the younger generation, a deep desire to escape the monotony and perpetual routine of the life of their parents and forefathers. Every major character wants to make some kind of difference in their lives and escape the stagnancy that surrounds them; some in constructive and helpful ways and some through seeking attention and infamy. The rest of the characters just seem to accept their fate and live for the rare special moments of feeling some sort of fleeting joy, a connection or purpose in life. The titular ‘Last Picture Show’ symbolises the only escape for most of these individuals in the form of a crumbling local cinema that is about to be closed down by its benevolent but sickly owner who himself represents the life of the town. As such the film is a meditation on loneliness, yearning, alienation and the desperate desire human beings have to connect with others by whatever means possible, a desire that becomes more intense the more isolated society is from the outside world. I would safely assume that all the actors read either the script (and/or the magnificent book by Larry McMurtry) understood the themes, did the assignment and delivered. Practically every scene is like a masterclass in acting. My personal favourite being the final scene where the teenaged protagonist Sonny returns, dejected and alienated, to the middle aged Ruth Popper. She herself has long suffered such feelings and they both share a moment, finally understanding one another; older and younger generation, with the gentle touch of hands. Around them the wind howls non stop in the background while the strain of the same old country songs, same old ads and same outdated radio shows play on the transistor behind them. This serves to remind them that this is their lives and there is little to nothing they can do to change it. This is a film that I believe anyone who lives (or has lived) in a location forgotten by the rest of the general population can relate to, regardless what part of world it is.

What are some inaccuracies or criticisms of JD Vance's book "Hillbilly Elegy"? Oh here we go again. So I'm supposed to assume this has nothing to do with the fact that Trump just appointed JD Vance as his running mate for Vice President. No. The person who asked the question is genuinely interested in a review of Vance's book and the question is in no way a negatively leading question. I haven't read the book yet but I saw the movie. I remember the movie was thrashed by critics and Hollywood acted as though Amy Adams should be drawn and quartered for taking part in such political, propagandist rubbish. The criticism was non stop. I almost believed what the media was saying. Then I watched it and was surprised to discover that it was a really good movie. It was just a simple story about a guy who struggled in life with poverty and drugs in his family and managed to make something of himself thanks to the two people who supported him in his life. The performances were excellent, particularly Amy Adams and Glenn Close and there was nothing remotely political or propagandist about the story. There is nothing in the book that merits me investigating the inaccuracies in the book. It is a memoir. Vance doesn't make any fantastic claims. It's not like Catch Me if You Can or My Wicked Wicked Ways. Did he exaggerate? Did his mother really overdose on heroin or was she just taking a nap? Is Vance's wife really of Indian descent or just three quarters Indian? Did Vance really drive all night to a job interview right after wrestling a heroin needle from his mother or did he just have a stern argument with her, took a nap and a plane the next morning? Does that matter? Are these the ‘inaccuracies’ that should make us condemn the book and Vance? It's astonishing how much the modern left have idealised themselves into believing that they are the final say in regards to everything. That they are never wrong. Any other opinions are stupid, racist or sexist. As a Trinidadian I sometimes argue with such people as to the reality of what goes on on in my country. People who've never even set foot in the country. When will they realize that the more arrogant they behave and the more they tell people what they ought to believe, think, say and feel, the more people will become disenchanted and start doing the opposite of what they suggest. I'm certain Vance's book and the film will see a surge in sales and streaming in the upcoming weeks. I might even come around to reading it, simply because so many critics angrily claim that I shouldn't.

Would Hollywood actor Brad Pitt have made it in old or classic Hollywood back in the day? Very interesting question. For the sake of simplification let's just assume that by Classic Hollywood you mean the Hays Code era of Hollywood whereas sex, nudity, graphic violence, rape etc could not be demonstrated in Hollywood films. (1934 — 1968) 1930s — 1940s Hollywood Hollywood in the aftermath of the Great Depression and the outbreak of the Second World War. This is the age of the Go-Getter and although silent movies are now obsolete, it's exaggerative stage acting style is still rampant. Audiences of this era are favorable towards a certain type of male screen presence. Popular actors of the era are mostly an embodiment of what were considered desirable, manly traits. This is the era of Clark Gable, Cary Grant, Gary Cooper, James Stewart, Errol Flynn, John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The archetypal male film star was usually tall (over 6 feet), athletic, handsome, possessing a rich and resonant voice and possessing a certain self assured alpha male quality. The kind of man who would've made a great career as a top salesman or workforce motivator. The nation was wounded after two World Wars and these idealistic tropes were coveted by men and women alike. It was an age that was obsessively preoccupied with courage, persistence and survival. It was the era of sucking in your emotions and holding your chin high. Unless in possession of exemplary acting skills or song and dance expertise, actors who lacked several of these traits were relegated to minor supporting roles, comic relief roles, extras, stunt work or failed to make it in the film industry at all. Despite being ruggedly handsome, Brad Pitt would've had a hard time getting work in Hollywood during this era. He did not fit the height requirement, his voice would not be considered rich and animated and his brooding, sombre presence would've been a turn off for a national audience hungry for the next cocky, high shouldered, go-getting macho man. 1950s Hollywood The ideal aforementioned leading man is still prevalent with Charlton Heston, Gregory Peck, Burt Lancaster, and Rock Hudson maintaining the status quo. However standards are less rigid as actors like William Holden, Frank Sinatra, Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner and Tony Curtis, who have the macho appeal but lack the height, are some of the top stars. A growing interest in brooding more sensitive type 'method' acting is gaining ground with the likes of James Dean, Marlon Brando and Paul Newman. Brad Pitt would've been better able to find work in such type roles but the competition would be fierce and only those with extensive stage experience and schooled in New York at the Actor's Studio would get top priority over some quiet, good looking guy from Missouri. 1960s Hollywood The growing counterculture revolution is finally making an impact on Hollywood. While the war scarred older generation is fading to make way for the Baby Boomers, the conservative values and ideal macho leading man is no longer as appealing for those hungry for emotional catharsis. The audience is yearning for a leading man who they could relate to, who shares their flaws and can demonstrate vulnerability. Even the more macho type actors are expected to demonstate weakness and more sensitivity. These would include Clint Eastwood, Sean Connery, Charles Bronson, Steve McQueen, Robert Redford, George Kennedy and Rod Steiger. Slurred speaking (Marlon Brando), meek voiced (Eastwood) overweight (Steiger) and short stature (Bronson) are traits no longer shunned by Hollywood elite. Brad Pitt would've found the greatest chance of obtaining prominent roles during this era. Who knows he might've even replaced Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

Which movie character do you feel sorry for? Miles Dyson: Terminator 2 Judgement Day If there is one casualty from a movie that literally brought tears to my eyes it had to be him. Just imagine that you're a mild mannered microprocessor expert employed for a big-tech company. You are passionate about your job and firmly believe that what you are doing will change the world for the better. While working at home with your wife and preteen son, a woman who just had a violent escape from a mental asylum carelessly empties several clips from a high powered machine gun into your house destroying your workstation and narrowly killing you and potentially causing fatal harm to your family. Then imagine being shot in the arm by the crazed gunwoman and looking on helplessly as she points a gun to you and your family while shouting obscenities and claiming 'It's all your fault.’ She doesn't kill you but she shows you a man wanted for a shootout in a mall who possesses a robotic arm. She tells you that you are the cause of the end of the world. She relates to you a fantastic story of time travel, having sex and producing a child with a man from the future. That her son eventually will become the saviour of the human race and a leader in an epic battle between humans and robots. You are forced to believe her because she has many guns, an emotionally overwhelmed mind and the assistance of a bodybuider with a robotic arm. She then forces you to break into the worklab and destroy all traces of your work and its related developments. In the process you are shot several times by inept police and your body is exploded into several pieces due to holding the detonator the bodybuilder makes you, a 100 pound pencil-necked geek, hold (even though he claims to be a near indestructable cyborg). Sarcasm aside, Dyson's death was sad because he was truly a nice guy with a conscience and a trusting and faithful nature. Kudos to the actor Joe Morton who provides a heartfelt performance full of pathos and leaves an impression on many of the fans of the movie. A pity his career didn't take off after this role. However, it was not Dyson's fault. Sarah's obsession with killing him as the cure for Judgement Day is one of the reasons I have ambiguous feelings towards her as a hero. It was very ignorant and immature of her to foster such primitive cause and effect type logic. It's very much like believing that by killing the guy who created gunpowder you can stop World War I and II from happening. It's also very cowardly of her to bully and assault the harmless and defenceless guy rather than take up her beef with the powerful Cyberdyne corporation, the real villains. No. Assault nerdy Dyson and his family, wrack his mind full of guilt and have him needlessly killed thanks to your crackpot plan. Poor Dyson.

What is the one topping that always ruins a pizza for you? Having worked six years doing part time delivery at a famous local pizza restaurant, I've seen the oddest of requests for custom made pizzas. Here are some noteworthy examples: However the most heinous crime one can commit with pizzas happens very regularly. You reading this probably have done it yourself as it is a common practice. Double (extra) cheese And in some cases triple cheese Whenever someone says those forbidden words, I say a prayer for these lost souls. Do they not realize that they are defeating the purpose and aesthetic beauty of consuming a pizza? Might as well order a bucket of fried chicken skins at KFC. Everything is lost in a messy gloop of cheese and (if cheddar) oil. Counter-argument: 'I order mozzarella and that isn't oily but is tender and stringy without overpowering the other ingredients.’ But excessive mozzarella can kill you instantly. Mozzarella has a tendency to get stuck in your throat and choke you like it did my girlfriend some years ago and several other people who related similar stories to me. A modest pizza slice has 285 calories. That sounds reasonable right. Two slices and that's 570 calories. No damage done. But you know you ain't eating just two slices. Three slices rounds you up at 855, a light dinner and wouldn't wake up the next morning looking like Jabba The Hutt. Let's just pretend that those awful carbs from flour that widen your midsection don't exist. Double cheese…..310 calories per slice. 3 slices and you are at 930 almost half the daily recommended calorie intake for the average female. That means a salad for dinner little missy. Now triple cheese it, doing the Math that would be 25 additional calories at 335 per slice. That would be 1005 for your three slices. Yeah but who wants just cheese on their pizza. Make it a Hawaiian: ham, bacon and pineapple. That bacon is a calorie assassin mind you and this rounds up to an additional 113 calories per slice which would make your 3 slices 1344. Wash it all down with a large Coke, 1483. Just ignore the oils and fats that are running into your arteries and bloodstream and the gluten enriched, hard to digest, immune system killing white flour and you will have good dreams. Doesn't seem so bad. A few months of doing this on a weekly basis and congratulations. You're not Jabba the Hutt but you look a lot like this. Not bad except that Jabba the Hutt at least had some more aesthetics and culture when it came to his food.

What is the luckiest thing that happened to you? Over twenty years ago I was a mere lad of 17 and staying at a cousin's house for the holidays. My aunt was fed up of us staying in the living room all day playing video games and sent us to walk the dogs. The area was a very safe upper middle class location fringed by mountains and a picturesque golf course nearby. My brother, myself and our cousin walked the quiet road calmly discussing our victories in the gaming world when suddenly we heard the ferocious growling and snapping of a giant pitbull which had broken off its owner’s iron chain and was heading towards us in a mad fury, saliva dripping from its mouth. We stood frozen, all three of us knowing fully well that we were going to get mauled. The minute the dog's feet touched the road a speeding pickup came out of nowhere knocked it on the head. The sound of the hit was loud and blood curdling. It literally sounded like a car crash. The force was enough to give instant death to a human yet the dog managed to run back to its house. The driver sped off without even a moment's thought as to what just happened. It was almost as though Jesus Himself was driving that pickup that saved us from getting severely mauled. We stood there petrified, not knowing what to do or say. Should we quickly head back home? Should we query with the owner as to whether the dog was alive? Should we make a report to the police? None of these logical things we did. Instead we had an argument as to whether the dog was alive or not, if it was, whether it was severely concussed or just fine and whether the skull of a pitbull was tougher than that of a human. My cousin, a lover of physics, then made an argument as to whether a pitbull as such, running at 130km an hour could ram into and overturn a small car. I opted out of this argument and took some time reflecting on the poor dog. I'm glad to be unscarred but to this day I hope the bugger didnt suffer too much.
