Have you ever met a dangerous person and not known it at the time? Maurice was a soft-spoken and mild mannered boy in my class. He was friendly and pleasant to all. I cannot think of a single moment where he said or did something that angered or offended anyone while in school. He lived further up the hill from where my school was; practically walking distance from the school. Girls confided in him due to his reserved nature and boys respected his kindness. Once he invited a few of us guys to his house for food and to watch SpiderMan (the very first movie) on his PC, after school. Maurice was the last boy one would think of when the word ‘dangerous’ was mentioned. When we entered Form 5, a boy named Kevin entered the school and stoke fear upon many of us. I say ‘boy’ but he was already an 18yo adult when he came. He had transferred from a really rough school and practically every week he was involved in vicious fights or would be seen breaking class to smoke behind the labs. He would harass random boys, threaten them for their money and if they didn't cough up he'd shove, slap or thrash them, according to his mood. Maurice happened to pass by him one day and judging Maurice to be harmless he tackled Maurice for some money. Maurice ignored him but Kevin grabbed him by the shirt and slapped him on both cheeks, warning him that next time things will be worse. Maurice's shirt was dirty and his face red from the fracas but he remained silent and walked away. After school ended I was walking with my friends out the compound and down the hill when we saw trouble was brewing. We saw a gang of no less than twenty young men from the area had accosted Kevin. Kevin's face was bruised and swollen, eyes red and most of his shirt buttons were ripped out from a prior struggle. They dragged Kevin to Maurice and asked what to do with him. Maurice, in his soft voice told them that that was enough. The men shoved Kevin off and fired kicks behind him as he ran down the hill, thoroughly learning his lesson. The hill where the school lay was Maurice's turf. Kevin learned a lesson that day. The most dangerous people are sometimes the ones you least suspect.

What's the most dishonest thing you've experienced in your working life? In a school I once worked there was on old curmudgeon who worked as a handyman. For simplicity’s sake I'll refer to him as Levi. Everything about him was dishonest. He was employed as a handyman but could barely repair anything. Any minor problem brought to him, he make it seem as though it were was a huge issue. We had a toilet that gave problems to flush. We told him about it and without flushing and inspecting it, he claimed that the entire toilet was broken and needed to be replaced. He actually managed to get the Principal to sign off on this and any other 'replace’ verdicts he claimed as he knew how to charm women in high positions. He would then 'discard’ of the old toilet or any other item that was replaced. He was a talker and a social butterfly. He would always rant about how hard his life was. He lived to blow smoke up people's asses. Whenever you saw him he always 'just came back from a smoke...' I interpreted this by mentally adding '…up someone's ass’ to his statement. Whenever anyone discussed work with him he would always say his mantra, 'There's no incentive here for me.’ Everyone knew he was corrupt and took advantage of the job and the Principal. Because he was a character with personality and didn't rip-off his fellow workers with his incentives, everyone still liked him. However his desire for more incentives was to get the better of us. The school had a hill of old, beaten up iron and aluminium student chairs. They were stored outside the building in the back. They were an eyesore for the school and especially for the Principal. The Principal wanted to get rid of them but because of auditing purposes she couldn't simply discard them without approval from her district supervisor and a whole bunch of red tape. Levi saw the hill of chairs as a goldmine. He would tell everyone how much it would be worth as scrap iron and made his ultimate incentive to be to get the permission to discard of those chairs. One day he came to me with a proposal. I had a pickup. He told me that the principal gave him permission to discard of the chairs. He wanted me to take them to the scrapyard and we'd split the money 50:50. Knowing that he was a con-artist I went to the Principal and asked if she indeed gave him permission. She confirmed it was true and if I could assist with the transport. I agreed to the proposal. Levi also hired one of the junior handymen for a flat rate. Myself and the junior handyman worked ourselves to the core stacking those chairs to the van and securing. Levi didn't lift a finger as he complained about his old age and his back. It took three trips with my pickup to carry all the chairs to the scrapyard. By the time we were done, the junior handyman and I were dripping in sweat. We waited outside the building to get our cut from Levi. When Levi finally came out he was shouting racial obscenities against the entire Chinese population. We asked him what happened. He said that the owner, a native of China, could barely speak English and inspected the entire haul with the conclusion of 'Iron no good. We want aluminium.’ Levi said that the Chinese owner didn't want the iron chairs, practically 95% of the the haul, but only the aluminium ones which had a higher market value. He said the owner wanted us to carry the iron ones back. Levi said he begged the man to take the iron chairs for whatever price he was willing to offer. We asked Levi how much money he got for the entire haul. Levi showed us $75TT from his wallet. We were stunned. I for one didn't believe Levi's story in the least. I went inside to talk to the owner. Unfortunately it was true that he barely spoke English. We couldn't understand each other and he simply said to me, 'Iron no good. Next time bring aluminium.’ Levi acted the most heartbroken of all. All that work for nothing. We split the money in three. The junior handyman lamented that he never worked so hard in his life for enough money to buy a pack of cigarettes. A few weeks later Levi stopped coming to work. When the school rang him he announced that he was taking early retirement. The principal called me into her office all of a sudden. 'Where are the chairs?’ she cried, 'The supervisor is coming tomorrow.’ I told her I didn't understand what she meant. She explained to me that she gave Levi permission to salvage whatever chairs he could from the pile, have them repaired and painted and in exchange he could 'discard’ the rest. I told her the arrangement Levi had with us and how we carried all the chairs to the scrapyard. She stared at me with fury. She asked me if I knew where Levi lived. I said no. She said her calls to him went straight to voice message. She cried that Levi was supposed to bring 23 refurbished chairs for her since last week. She even had the figure listed in the school inventory. I didn't know what to tell her. I said I would try to find out any information I could. I called the scrapyard to find out if they had any information on him: a second phone number, an address etc. Thankfully the Chinese owner had a English speaking person employed as a CSR. I asked the CSR about Levi and whether she has any information on him. She looked up our sale in the computer. She said Levi made the transaction under the school's name and phone number but left no personal information on himself other than his first name. I then found out that the sale of the chairs as scrap amounted to almost $3000TT. Levi had ripped everyone off, myself, the junior handyman, the Principal and the school. Big time. Looks like he had finally gotten his incentive.

What is the strangest complaint you have received at your job? Some years ago while counting down the last few minutes before my shift ended in a public library, a young woman came to the information desk with an ennraged look on her face. Lady: Can someone please tell me where the Spanish classes are? I've been on all the floors and no one seems to know what I'm talking about. Me: Sorry miss but those aren't Spanish classes. The Spanish Embassy has been having a series of public talks every Wednesday at 5 - 6 pm on the third floor discussing the Latin American economy. We simply allow them to use our conference room on the third floor. Lady: Are you listening to what I'm saying? I left work early to come to these Spanish classes. Where are the people for the Spanish class? Me: I'm sorry miss but we really don't know. We simply give the Embassy access to our conference room. You might want to call the number they left on the advertisement. Lady: So you're saying this is your library, where you work, but you have no idea what's going on? Me: We know all what is going on in regards to our public services but the Embassy's program is something external. Any complaints about the program can be addressed to the Embassy's website. Lady: Typical lazy government worker mentality…So you're saying you have no knowledge of what is going on in your own building? Me: This is actually not our building. Several government departments are housed in this building besides the library. Would you like me to call the Embassy for you? Lady: You've wasted my time already. It's already 5:30pm. I mean does it feel good to you to be getting paid for nothing? What's the point of this library? I want to speak to your manager. I was about to explain to her that we don't have ‘managers’ but librarians when she whips out her cell phone and shows a screenshot of a Facebook post advertising the Embassy's program. Me: Miss. I'm sorry but that post shows that the program ends April 24th, which was two weeks ago… Lady: ……so you….this is so unprofessional…..a big freaking library and you can't call people and tell them that the Spanish class program has finished. I want to speak to the manager. This is unacceptable. It was at this point I decided I that I no longer waste my time with this lady's nonsensical complaint.

What is the stupidest assumption you ever made? Several years ago I worked as a warehouse attendant for a major distribution company. It was my first job. Every year, usually in September, we had our annual stock-taking exercise. It was bittersweet because though it was hard work (especially for the males who did all the climbing and counting every single product in the warehouse whilst females wrote figures on the notepad) there would usually be a lot of the beautiful Head Office women present and we would be treated to lunch by the Director. We were all randomly assigned one partner. On our notice board they would put the name of our randomly allocated mystery partner. Of course many of the virile and single young men like myself hoped and prayed to be partnered with a stunning beauty from the Head Office. When the list was put up I saw that my partner was ‘Vanessa Milan.’ I jumped high into the air in excitement. VANESSA MILAN What a name! I envisioned a tanned beauty from a Mediterranean island, tall and shapely with arched eyebrows, a sensuous mouth and curly jet, black hair. In other words I imagined a Sophia Loren look-alike. I began bragging to my male friends that Vanessa Milan and I would probably be secretly in each others arms embracing behind a pallet of goods whilst they would be walking on eggshells with their nagging, old-maid partners. Every time I mentioned Vanessa Milan’s name I said it in a low whisper as though she were the Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I drove my co-workers crazy uttering her exotic name every day. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I laughed at some of the names my friends were paired with: ‘Penny Thomas….Ha…..That sounds like a big, fat mama.’ ‘Giselle Aleong….she sounds like a bony psycho.’ And comments to that extent (I was 19 years old). One of my friends Rory advised me that I was a fool. That nothing could be more stupid than guessing what someone is like based on their name. I replied, ‘True, But a name like Vanessa Milan has to be an exotic beauty. Who ever heard a name like Vanessa Milan in this country?’ When the day came for the stock-take, all of us guys stood in the open area of the warehouse and observed a wide array of beauties from the Head Office. The Director gathered us all together for a prayer and then called out the names of the allocated partners for us to team up. Penny Thomas was a straight up knock-out. Giselle Aleong, with a body like that, could’ve graced the cover of Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Edition. I looked stunned as she walked by with my friend Rory (her assigned partner) who had warned me about my assumptions. He looked at me with a faint, mocking smile. When Vanessa Milan’s name was called, (the Director blasphemously screeched her name in her guttural voice) no one answered. All my friends stared at me as they were in great suspense to finally see this exotic mystery woman I boasted about all week. Suddenly, a dumpy, middle-aged lady with bad posture and Coke bottle specs that made her look like someone’s mom from the 60’s came hurriedly into the clearing. ‘I’m here. I’m here,’ she cried in a mournful voice. I was taken aback. Sophia Loren she wasn’t. She looked and acted more like Pat from the It’s Pat SNL sketch. Awkwardly I shook hands with her and stared at the ground. She began to relate a woeful tale of how she wasn’t feeling well that morning and was running late as she sped up the road driving but had forgotten to feed her dog so she had to drive back home and that was why she was late and on and on and on she went relating woeful, semi-depressing tales for me while we were doing our stock checks. ‘One hundred and seventy five cases of Diquez Baby Oil 125ml!’ I shouted down at her from a pallet of goods on the shelf above her, ‘Did you get that?’ ‘Oh sorry,’ she said, ‘I can’t hear you. I have bad hearing in my right ear. Ever since I was…..’ ‘ONE-SEVEN-FIVE CASES……DIQUEZ BABY OIL…….125ML, ‘ I shouted at the top of my lungs. This was the third time in thirty minutes this type of communication problem happened and I was getting frustrated. Part of it was my selfish and immature disappointment at her not being the beauty I imagined but alas she was so whiny and helpless. ‘I can’t hear you.’ she replied woefully, ‘I think we should go ask the Director if the Manager has any walky-talkies around.’ ‘WE DON’T HAVE ANY WALKY-TALKIES IN THE WAREHOUSE,’ I screamed at her but she already left to find the Director while I stood suspended 30 feet above the ground on a shelf waiting on her. In the end I had to count the stock and write in the figures myself as she followed me about apologizing at every turn. After the momentous day passed, for weeks my friends and co-workers would tease me. They would breathlessly whisper her name whenever I passed. ‘Vanessa Milan. Mi amore. Mi amore.’ Thus ended the saga of Vanessa Milan, My Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love.

What harsh truth did you learn as a teenager? There was a boy named Sid in my class in Secondary (High) school. He was an odd boy and a bit of a loner. He was the guy who'd always 'kill the joke’ in class i.e. when everyone in class starts making funny comments about someone or something, he was the one that would make an awkward, completely unrelated comment that killed and buried the laughter. He was one of the few boys to have a full moustache at the age of 12 and the one day he shaved it off he looked like he came from another planet and was the laughing stock of the week. I used to feel sorry for him but sometimes he'd say the darndest things that were so bizarre and unfunny that I couldn't help but shake my head and sigh. Even some of the teachers would groan at some of the unfunny attention seeking statements that Sid would make. Biology teacher: So that's why female dogs produce multiple babies whereas female humans usually produce one. Sid: So why didn't God give female dogs multiple vaginas to make it easy on them. These kind of statements, along with a collective sigh from the class would be the routine for years to come. This was until suddenly I witnessed Sid make an unfunny joke and all of a sudden most of the kids in class started laughing. Then I noticed the teachers started behaving favorably towards him; feigning laughter at his silliness and giving him special attention and help in class Then I noticed two of the most desired girls in school were fighting over him, both of them vociferously declaring to be his true girlfriend. Nobody made fun of him and even the worst bullies and class clowns made sure not to mess with him. I wondered if the world had gone mad. I discussed it with my friends and they explained it to me. 'Didn't you hear? Sid's rich.’ As it turned out Sid's father was a prominent lawyer in the country. Nobody realized this until he visited the school for a parent's day. Having connections to a rich and powerful lawyer was something our dilapidated and poorly funded school coveted and as such Sid was now treated like royalty. For his 16th birthday he was given a new car and he proudly drove it into the compound with his two girlfriends inside; the only boy in the school's history to have that luxury. However he was still as corny and awkward as ever but no one seemed to pay that any mind. So the harsh truth I learned as a teenager was: Money and power can make any donkey look like a stallion. Not Sid. Definitely not as rich. But a striking resemblance.

Was Shelley Duvall considered attractive? When I was a boy growing up, this character was the epitome of ‘attractive’ among boys my age: This was the exact opposite: Now that I'm a full grown adult I find it odd that my attraction has reversed. Nowadays I would consider prime Shelley Duvall far more attractive than prime Pamela Anderson. I'm not saying this as a form of virtue signalling due to her sad passing. I've observed photos from her in the past and discovered that she possessed a very unique beauty. This beauty was exploited quite often in her roles and modeling in the 1970s. Sadly she was only given frumpy housewife and plain Jane supporting roles into the 80s and 90s and all but disappeared at the turn of the millenium, only resurfacing for that infamous Dr. Phil interview in 2016. Despite being tall and thin, with big ears and eyes and crooked teeth Shelley Duvall’s looks were all natural. This might be my personal opinion but she seemed to possess a certain humility about her; the kind of person who wouldn't put on airs about herself and be friendly to almost anyone. Pamela Anderson’s beauty involved a lot of plastic surgery, hair dye and excessive makeup. To each his own but in a hypothetical party full of people I'd make a bee line to be the first to offer a drink to Shelley Duvall. Then we'd talk, sit and laugh at all the hopelessly shallow guys flocking around Pamela Anderson at the other end of the room. RIP

Which supporting actress was much more memorable than the star of a movie? Toni Collette gave one of the greatest performances ever rendered on film in the soon to be cult classic Hereditary (2018) but another actress outshined her by a fraction of a fraction. Ann Dowd gave a most chillingly deceptive performance of Joan, a warm and empathetic older lady who befriends Collette's character Annie as she struggles with tragedy, resentment and depression. The beauty of Ann's performance is her complex nuances. She transforms from a lovable, nurturing Aunt May type character that was so understated yet genuinely compassionate to a different being one would've never predicted her to be near the ending. The most common description I've heard about her character for those who've enjoyed the film is how 'real’ Joan seemed. Ann Dowd is one of the most underrated actresses of the 21st century. No one can play matriarchal type figures like her and even the most hardened scoundrel would find themselves letting down their guards and engaging a sense of love and trust in the warmth she emanates. Therefore it's startling when that different side of her comes out during the final 20 minutes of the film. I'm not giving spoilers because YOU NEED TO GO SEE HEREDITARY IF YOU HAVENT SEEN IT YET.

I have a fiance who is living in Portugal. I met him in a dating site, and we communicate in my WhatsApp. I want to video call him, but he said Portugal is banned in video calls. Is that true? My 66 year old Aunt had similar circumstances. Recently divorced and living alone far from any family in Ontario she was befriended online by a guy claiming to be working in the US Army. For months they have a back and forth on WhatsApp. She constantly asking for him to take some time to visit her, he constantly reminding her that his army duties don't all for him to vacation as often as he'd like. He also refused all WhatsApp audio and video calls because, according to him, it would compromise the US Army. However he did send her a photo of himself. Coincidentally if you search ‘US Army Officer Facebook’ on Google you can easily come across his photo. He assured her that when he does come and see her he would do so while flying through the skies in the Army helicopter and he would most definitely land in her apartment parking lot and take her up for a ride. She became smitten by him and he asked for her hand in marriage. She agreed but not long after he explained that he was tied up in a court battle over unpaid child support. According to him he had a mission in Somalia and had a rendezvous with one of the local women who eventually got pregnant for him and gave birth to son. My aunt, being as scrupulous as she is, asked for photo evidence of this child. He sent her this thumbnail. Coincidentally his son's photo could be found by simply searching ‘cute Somalian boy’ on Google. Nevertheless my aunt was convinced by his evidence and impressed by the cuteness of his son. Her Army boyfriend persuaded her to send $5000 CAD to the child's mother's Somalian bank account. After she did as such (and after being a bit wary as to why he was so adamant to remind her to send it on a daily basis) she stopped recieving messages from him. She came to the conclusion that she was scammed. It deeply hurt her and embarassed her and caused her sons and ex husband to stop sending her any large sums of money. However luck would have it that she befriended through Facebook a Swedish doctor of Indian descent. While discovering that he came into inheritance of a large sum of money he asked for her hand in marriage. Unfortunately, while on his way to see her he was held by Belgian authorities in regards to his large stash of gold in his suitcase in which he's now asking my aunt for help with his legal fees. Because of this unique situation he is unable to send or receive WhatsApp video calls. No matter how much we've tried to convince my aunt to drop this obvious scam she wouldn't listen. Anyway my point being is that whenever you meet some exotic character online who tells you some wacky story with claims that can be disproved with a simple Google search, it is with 100% certainty that person is trying to scam you.

Why is reading so important? Imagine this. You are with some friends on a fishing excursion in the Mediterranean sea. Miles away from the nearest harbor your yacht begins to sink. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) Another scenario. You are in a cabin in the Swiss Alps. An avalanche occurs and buries your cabin under twenty feet of snow. Your phone has enough juice to make one call. Who do you call? A) B) Final scenario. You have been drugged unconscious and abducted by traffickers who want to harvest your organs. Your kidnappers are taking you to a foreign land in which you cannot decipher the language, pinpoint the culture or recognize the terrain. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) If you chose ‘B’ for all the scenarios, congratulations, you are alive. If you chose ‘A’ for any scenario, you are most likely dead. The characters pictured under 'A’ are men who are extremely well-read. Ken Jennings — Record holder for the longest winning streak on Jeopardy. Karl Marx — Founding father of Marxism, a proponent of communism. Bill Nye — A mechanical engineer and popular television presenter, comedian and educator. The characters pictured under ‘B’ are men who are extremely well-read but also have a lot of worldly experience. Joseph Conrad — Polish born English author, explorer and ship captain. Jack London — American author, sailor, journalist and former Klondike prospector. Richard Francis Burton — English explorer, translator, linguist, historian and writer. This is not slight against the achievements of the characters under 'A’ it's just that the fellows under 'B’ have allowed for the knowledge they've amassed through reading to inspire them towards physical action which in turn develops experience and skill. Ken Jennings and Bill Nye might be able to tell you what is the distance of each planet in the Solar system from the sun in less than a minute but that doesn't mean NASA would aggressively pursue them. Marx, if he were alive, could write a 1000 page book on why he thinks 20th century communism failed but do you think Maduro or Castro would’ve employed him as an advisor? Group A are individuals of impressive intelligence but any logical thinking individual would recognize that Group B is superior in regards to worldly applicability. So to answer the question, reading is important to gain knowledge. Reading is very important, but not as important as the ACTION that it stimulates.

What is an example of someone who underestimated the wrong individual? In my first year of secondary (high) school, taunting and chest-beating was a norm amongst the more silly and immature boys like myself. Balram was an Indian boy who came from rural poverty. He wore worn clothes, kept an outdated hairstyle and mostly kept to himself to avoid the others making fun of him (which they constantly did). They would call him bush-coolie, Mowgli, Balram of the Jungle and various other insulting names. Balram would sit and deflect their insults with the stoic calmness of a Navajo chief. He was an acquaintance of mine but we were not close. However a group of boys looking to make a ruckus started taunting me that I was so weak, even bush boy Balram could beat me up, I quickly took to the offence. I rushed up to Balram who anticipated that I would fall for the bait and before I could say 'Bal’ he pinned me against the wall with two sinewy hands against my shoulders and told me to behave myself. Everyone was astonished at Balram's strength. After struggling to escape his grip for a several seconds he saw I was worn out and released me. That day forward I never messed with Balram and even became his good friend. The class still teased him, but this time they made sure they were at a safe distance when doing so.

Is it morally wrong to want to read Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf? I’ve no desire to read it but if someone suggested that by reading it, it would prove that I’m secretly a neo-Nazi then I would have a hearty laugh. I’ve read Venus is Furs. I’m not a masochist or into any form of BDSM. I’ve read The Doors of Perception. I haven’t ingested LSD nor have I been tempted. I’ve read Trainspotting. I’m not in the least bit curious to try heroin or any drug 1000 times more powerful than my greatest orgasm. Read The Stranger and Crime and Punishment. I was never tempted to kill someone for the heck of it. Read The Sun Also Rises and I still hate bullfighting to this day. Read all the Harry Potter novels and I'm still not inspired or influenced by witchcraft. I've read Lolita. I don't sympathise with pedophiles and hebephiles. I've read 1984. I think my Government is way too stupid to suppress my thoughts and actions. My point is I've read these books because I enjoy reading. If I don't enjoy the story, find it uninteresting or dislike the author's writing I simply put the book down. The only people who will get influenced by Mein Kampf or any of the books I've listed above are people who already believe the values and ideas they think the book suggests. The book is simply greater affirmation (or for some people, a good excuse) for enacting on these desires.

Have you ever walked out of an interview? I didn’t walk out but I sure pissed the hell out of them and made it as awkward as possible. A cable company was looking for part time sales reps for their dishes. I already had a full time job but was looking for a sideline. They arranged for the interview to be at 9am. I came an hour early to their main office. The security had a sour look in his face and asked me what it is I wanted. I told him my name and that I had an interview for 9am. He looked at me as though I was talking jibberish and simply muttered that he didn’t know anything about that and directed me to the payments/customer service area to ask one of the people there where to go. I ignored the queue and walked directly towards the agents and the guard comes frantically running to me like a mama bird protecting its nest. ‘Follow instructions,’ he grunted loudly, ‘I told you to join the line.’ I wanted to bark at him that he never told me that and that he had to be the worse security guard I’ve ever encountered in my life, but of course that wouldn’t bear well for my interview. Suddenly a short pretty young lady passing by looked at me and said, ‘You’re Mr. Williamson?’ I said yes and she told me to follow her to the waiting area. She was professional but I found her a tad too detached. She didn’t ask me about my trip here or apologize for the confusion or anything. She led me to a corridor and and told me to sit by a row of chairs and that the sales supervisor would see me in a moment. She went into a room and came out with a tall, attractive lady with curly hair who looked no older than 24. They passed me without a glance and I assumed that they were both sales people. While sitting there a bunch of people kept passing and no one seemed to recognize my existence. They were all salespeople and mostly men. They came in to use the company phones to try and close sales and make a bunch of noise laughing and hooting afterwards with one another. Something about the vibe of the place just didn’t sit well with me. Around 9:45am the two young ladies passed by me again and without a word went back into the room they had left prior. A few minutes later the shorter one came out and called me in. She said the supervisor was ready to see me. I came in and saw a simple table in front of me where the tall girl sat with her fingers clasped staring at me. The shorter one sat to the side of her and they beckoned me to sit. Just looking at them I could sense that they were ladies who treated themselves well. Their clothes looked expensive, hair, nails and skin well treated, designer handbags etc. They were both very attractive and they knew it. The taller one proceeded to talk about sales and asked what the word ‘sale’ means to me. I kept mentioning how I prefer customer satisfaction rather than soliciting a sale and each time I did that she paused and reverted back to talking about how this job is concerned with hard selling and customer satisfaction can’t come if you don’t have customers. ‘We focus on sales only’ the shorter one chimed in. In my mind I sarcastically said to myself, ‘That’s a shocker.’ They then started discussing targets. They showed me a list of all the packages they were selling. They wanted to get the most expensive packages sold because they believe that people weren’t aware of how much better these were. They wanted to know if I had a problem focusing on selling only the expensive packages this month. They wanted me to lie and say basic packages were unavailable at the moment and that the next month I can sell basic like normal. I was starting to find them and this whole place tiresome. They clearly had values different from mine and I could see myself having spats with them in no time. I decided that I wanted out. However I wasn’t one to walk out on interviews as word gets around in this tiny country. I started asking about pay. ‘Commissions’ the taller one said. ‘Aren’t there any paying jobs,’ I replied, ‘With like a salary.’ They both looked at each other and the taller one replied that there were but that was a different division. I started telling them how I bought a dish from this company some years ago and how I thought it was garbage. I then said that my skills were so good that I could sell thousands of those garbage dishes to people who didn’t even have televisions. They both remained silent. I then said that I only worked on weekends and I don’t answer calls between 8 - 4 pm. They both looked at each other. ‘So Mr. Williamson’ the taller one said with a smile, ‘That’s the end of our interview. Thank you for your time and we’ll be contacting you before the end of the week.’ Without bothering to shake hands I headed out of the room like a man with a bladder control problem. Regardless to say I got a formal email from them a week later civilly explaining that I was unsuccessful with the interview.

What do fast food employees think of customers who come in frequently, say, multiple times a week or even daily? Thank you, whomsoever asked this beautiful question. Working as a delivery rider for a popular pizza restaurant it was fascinating how the regular customers seemed to be at polar extremes. There was hardly a middle ground. The regulars were either exceedingly pleasant i.e. the ever smiling, courteous customer who knew you by name, empathized with you, were patient and just radiated warmth and kindness. I would refer to them as the sweethearts. Or there were the ones who saw fast food personnel as a cheap means to vent their personal frustrations, felt entitled (because they believed the company would not survive without them), always tried to 'beat the system,’ always cheap, petty and discourteous and always naturally doing something aggravating to everyone around them e.g. taking up two parking spaces, refusing to sit and wait for the order (standing impatiently by the cashier with folded arms and sullen face) and giving details as to all the operational flaws they've witnessed with the restaurant whilst preaching how they would fix these flaws if they owned the restaurant. I would refer to these as the soul-eaters. Unfortunately I can only distinctly remember the experiences with soul-eaters. Here are three fascinating accounts. The Coffee Boys. Every Saturday night a group of preppy young men, all between the ages of 18 — 20 would come to the restaurant. There were usually five of them and they would occupy an entire table. They would sit at this table for more than an hour regardless if they had long finished their meal, denying that space for other diners. What was the meal they each ordered that merited leasing the table for such an extended period of time: One cup of coffee. That didn't bother any of us. It's not our restaurant, the company has no policy against such an obvious loss-incurring action and we were trained that the customer is always right. What made them unlikable was how they went about ordering their single cup of coffee. The ringleader, the most preppy of them all, would do the ordering. Despite being just some 18yo kid just off of cricket practice, he would speak to you as though he's the son of the owner of the restaurant. 'Things are pretty slow for the hour huh…..Susan?’ 'Patrice…… Are those cookies fresh or are they from the morning batch?’ 'Looks like you need a new shirt huh…… Phillip?’ He would always call out your name from your name tag, not as a show of courtesy, but in an authoritative almost passive-aggressive manner. After a minute or two of his condescending conversation, he would request 5 coffees with cream, literally the cheapest item on the menu. The cashier would pour them out in cups, neatly cover them with lids and place them on a tray. The words 'thank you’ or even subtle gesture of appreciation would never emanate from him as he would eye the cups, lift a cup to his face, remove a lid, sniff at coffee and take a sip in a manner as though he is the ultimate connoisseur of generic fast food coffee. 'Ummm. Maria?’ he would say to the cashier after taking his sip. The cashier would nod and come to him. He would then continue, 'Something is up with this coffee…I think you need to check your coffee machine.’ Then a hullabaloo would ensue with different members of staff tasting the coffee, not finding anything wrong. The manager would come out and taste the coffee and find no fault with it. However coffee-boy is not satisfied until he sees the coffee machine opened up to reveal that there is indeed sufficient powdered coffee and creamer in the machine. The five original cups of coffee are discarded and the cashier has to keep adjusting the machine and pouring out coffee, giving coffee-boy a sample to taste until he finds it is just right. Five fresh cups of coffee are then poured and he goes to his gang to occupy the table for over an hour after having caused over $50 worth of wasted coffee and cups. The Church Group. Once a month, on a Sunday night a large group of people who just finished worshiping at a nearby church would come into the restaurant. Their orders would be large, usually ranging between 4 — 6 family sized pizzas. They were courteous, patient and would attempt to be friendly. However they never failed to infuriate us all whenever they came. Firstly they would always come just a few minutes before closing time to place a big order. Though they could've easily called pick up an hour in advance, they preferred to come when we've already washed up the dishes and mopped the floor, anxiously waiting the closing time. 'I'm sorry but we've closed off dining for the night as we are about to close. You could only have the order as a take-away.’ the cashier would tell them. 'Oh well,' the pastor of the group would say, 'Well then we'll have to forget about the order.’ He's saying this but he knows that we cannot refuse a large order no matter how near it is to closing time. He knew that if the head office got wind of our branch refusing a $500+ order, we would be reprimanded. He knows all this but he is pretending to show humility for his church congregation. The cashier would acquiesce and remind the pastor that in ten minutes time we would be closing. The pastor would smile and assure the cashier that they wouldn’t be long. Staff would have to reheat the ovens, gather all the dough and ingredients that were neatly packed away in the chillers and grudgingly prepare these pizzas, knowing fully well that the order would be finished beyond our closing hour, after which we would have to wait for the church group to finish their meal. The restaurant would close at 10 pm on a Sunday. The church group would get their meal at around that time. Even though we’ve already tucked away the chairs and neatly aligned the tables for the next day, the church group would drag about a couple tables and join them together. Anything that is request-able you bet your bottom the group would request it; more napkins, more cups with ice, more condiments, turn off the air condition please, OK its too warm now, can you turn it back on, mini boxes to carry home leftovers, plastic bags, can this pizza be warmed over? etc, etc. While they are eating, the pastor, though he knows that he promised he will not stay long is encouraging members of the group to share tame, inoffensive church-based jokes and stories. All of us would and listen as Mrs. Nora recounted the time when she sent her grandson to get Communion bread but he didn't remind her that he wasn't a confirmed Catholic yet; how she gave him a good licking that evening when they returned home. The pastor howled with laughter. We would then interrupt their laughter to explain to them that we were ready to lock the building. The pastor would act surprised and apologize for losing track of time. We would wait another 10 minutes as they scrambled to distribute leftovers and gather their belongings. They wouldn’t even bother to help tidy back the area because they are now suddenly concerned about overstaying their time. They all apologized and thanked us for being so patient with them. We would then have to clean up all their spills, stains, used napkins, cups, pizza boxes and trays, re-wipe the tables, re-mop the floor and reposition the tables and chairs. We would lock the restaurant and when we exited the building the church group would be outside hanging about near their vehicles, continuing their conversation. Most of us didn’t have vehicles and would struggle that late hour to get a taxi as the streets would be near-deserted. None of the church group members would even consider offering us a ride as they left the restaurant in their cars. The Pool Guy. Lastly, there was a guy who would come in every day after work to place the same order of a mini pizza with chicken. I can’t remember his name but he would always mention to whomsoever was cashing that he was ‘building his pool.’ That pool must’ve been deeper than the Atlantic Ocean because for years he would always mention that pool that he was building. I can say without the slightest doubt that pool-guy was an asshole. I’m not even going to try to be subtle about it. He was a certified piece of s**t. Of all the scummiest people I’ve met on this Earth, he ranks in the top 5. Pool guy was a short hairy guy in his mid to late 30’s with a head full of graying hair. He always had a disheveled, resentful look as though he just woke up from a sleepless night with a terrible hangover. He was always making threats, harassing or trying to intimidate the mostly female workers to get some sort of preferential treatment i.e. being served before everyone else, getting more toppings on his pizza etc. Such tactics were common on an everyday basis but what set pool guy apart was that he naturally wanted to piss you off and provoke you to the limits of what is legally allowed. Pool guy definitely had some personal problems in his life and saw the restaurant as a means to vent his anger and frustration. Pool guy seemed as though he couldn’t overcome certain obstacles/people in his life so instead he would channel this anger into abusing a bunch of hapless, minimum wage earning women in a fast food restaurant. His tactic was that he would enter the restaurant and with no common courtesy he would gruffly order his mini pizza with chicken. He would remind the cashier at what time he placed his order and would subtly threaten that waiting makes him angry and we really don’t want to see him when he’s angry. He would then stand with arms folded, hearing distance away from the cashier, refusing to take his seat until he got his order. Most of us knew that he didn’t really care about the order. He got his thrill in harassing and psychologically abusing the more timid female staff at the front counter. ‘Go check on my order,’ he would demand every couple of minutes, ‘I’m waiting too long.’ Nothing thrilled him more than when his order took longer than the standard 15 minutes. Now he had an excuse to abuse. ‘Where is my order?’ he would shout. If no one answered him he would use this as an excuse to become vile. ‘ Like there’s only stupid, slow and uneducated people working in here?’ or ‘If I was your ‘child-father’ (baby-daddy) you would’ve moved faster.’ or ‘You could be a disappointment to your family but don’t disappoint me here today.’ The most pathetic thing about pool guy was that he would never dare behave like that in the presence of other customers. He would step away when a queue of customers were around and when they dispersed, like a rat coming out of his hole he would return to provoke and insult. There was never a single moment where he displayed a likable side to him. When he was in a good mood, he wouldn’t threaten and abuse but he would instead rant about his achievements in life. He claimed that he owned a fleet of trucks and his family were of great wealth and status that they practically owned the entire North coast of Trinidad. He would talk about how he traded in his cars every five years, that he spent over 5 million on his house in the past three years and how he was thinking of widening the pool that he had under construction and choosing a different set of tiles than what he originally intended I never met another delivery rider who didn’t feel like punching pool guy’s face in after being forced to listen to one of these boastful and selfish conversations. What is the common parenting mistake and how can they rectify that? The worst parenting mistake is not showing any genuine love to your children. The most common parenting mistake ironically is to constantly be selflessly giving to them. I see it more as a source of vanity and pride rather than of genuine love. I have three relatives who are from such a household. Their parents are well-off and stable with the mother supplying them an abundance of love and the father an abundance of money whenever the time calls. All three of them are in their 40s and do not live in the same country as their parents. They come to see their parents every Christmas as a tradition. This sounds nice of them, for all three of them to arrange a date to arrive and stay at the family home, plane tickets etc. In reality their parents are the ones who see to that. The parents have been paying for their children to come see them for Christmas for over twenty years. The parents arrange the date, the tickets and additional expenses that their 40 something year old children may accrue during their stay. Some readers may not see a problem with this. If you can afford it, why not treat your kids, especially during the Christmas? My answer to them is that it has nothing to do with money. It has to do with principle. No one should have to pay to see their grown children once a year. If your kids really cared about you they would come on their own volition and expense, not wait for daddy to purchase highly inflated Christmas flights. Not only this but the parents (both in their 70s) are the one to pick them up upon arrival and drop them off for departure. The parents also provide them with a New Year's vacation to a hotel every year and pay all expenses associated with it. The parents cook meals, carry them out for lunch/dinner and arrange all forms of planning and entertainment. To say that their kids are somewhat spoiled would be quite an understatement. To say that their kids were concerned about their parents descent into old age, loss of movement/stamina and increasing loneliness would be a great exaggeration. This arrangement is likely to continue until one of their parents die of which I'm certain the other parent would have to buy their tickets so they can attend the funeral. When you train your kids that they can receive a constant supply of love without them having to reciprocate you are training them to expect love without having to reciprocate. This is almost as damaging as showing no love at all.

What are the cleverest scams you have come across? Take a breath, grab a coffee if you may, and allow me to explain to you why we are called 'Tricky-dadians’ by the rest of the Caribbean. Band Ladies Around 2016 — 2018 a phenomenon occurred where sightings of these cultish ladies in heavy clothing similar to that of traditional Amish females were found throughout Trinidad. They were typically spotted at commercial areas such as malls and PriceSmarts (Costco) mostly at the parking lot. They were renowned for asking for your assistance with the rebuilding of their church. They claimed to do this with the purchase of their cheap rubber hand bands of which they would charge anything upwards of $20TT. If you refused to buy their generic, overpriced bands they would then initiate Phase 2 of their scheme which would be to overwhelm the victim with guilt with a pathos laden statement of 'Or maybe you could contribute just a small donation. Anything?’ They employed great acting skills and for many, seeing these harmless women in humble, old fashioned garb being constantly refused and rejected for their worthy cause tugged a few heartstrings. However, as with most scams, they got too greedy too fast. Their monthly appearances soon turned to weekly and then daily. Rather than target one location for the day and wrap up afterwards, it soon became clear that they began employing routes. A typical Band Lady route would be PriceSmart Chaguanas till 2pm, Trincity Mall until 6pm and PriceSmart Mausica until 9pm. They were noticed and mentioned by some of the populace but being that they were always pleasant and took 'no’ graciously, no one bothered to think twice about their scheme. However, the last straw was a rather desperate appearance at a CPL T20 cricket match (above photograph). Trinidad is very tolerant of beggars and we throw a blind eye towards scammers for the most part but for the Band Ladies, plying their scheme in the middle of a regional cricket match where national pride was at a peak, created an online outcry. Everyone suddenly posted a story, photo or recording of a dubious encounter with one of these Band Ladies and from that moment on they were no longer seen in public. Warning *Foul language*

Did gamers in the 90s think that the game graphics at the time were super realistic? 90s gamer here. It was rare to find a realistic game in the 90s so ‘super realistic’ was never a phrase 90s gamers would use when describing the graphics. Mortal Kombat (1992) was probably the first game whereby its realism was remarked upon by society to the point where it became infamous for its violence and gratuitous gore captured with real life human models. It’s almost laughable now that such stiff characters executing caveman like fight moves with dubious physics and anatomy created such a moral outcry back in 90s. Technology was limited back in the day that whenever game developers tried their hardest at realistic graphics great sacrifices had to be made. Gran Turismo (1997) had the most graphically precise 3D cars (for its time) but the graphics for practically everything else in the game was shite. The Virtua Fighter, Tekken and Dead or Alive franchises created awesome human\humanoid characters that looked somewhat realistic (especially in cut scenes) but looked clunky and zombie like while fighting. It was the norm for laughable physics such as characters seemingly floating in the air while jumping/falling or a mere kick to the shin making an opponent’s entire body contort as though struck with a sledgehammer. Don’t even mention the bland, lifeless backgrounds with beaches, canyons, temples and bridges as wide as a football field. No one I knew ever sat and praised the realism of graphics of such games. Graphics were usually referred to as good or bad in the 90s. It was in the late 90s was when gamers really began to praise realistic graphics. Metal Gear Solid (1998) is the PlayStation title that held unanimous praise for solid graphics (as well as sound, physics, perspective etc) throughout. There was hardly a sour note in its execution and most gamers I know had that ‘felt as if I was there’ feeling while playing the game. The limitation with Metal Gear was that practically every level looked like a replica of the last with snowy blue/green military compounds/laboratories being the general motif. The Sega Dreamcast arrived in 1998 and rather than good or bad, realistic graphics became a major talking point. Soul Calibur (1998) erased all the clunky eeriness of its 3D beat ‘em up predecessors. However the game that took realism as close to super realism graphically and gameplay-wise was Shenmue (1999). As laughable and meme worthy Shenmue has become now, it was seen as the beacon for games of the future. Controlling every action and decision of the protagonist in a sprawling, well rendered Yokosuka Japan, full of interactive and dynamic human characters, it was as close as one could get to virtual reality at the time. The graphics were gorgeous for its time; seeing old women dusting shop fronts, falling rain, men puttering about on mopeds and petals floating about in the wind made it one of the first games to embrace cinematography. Were it not for the gratuitous cut scenes/camera angles, uncanny valley faces and goofy dubbing Shenmue would’ve been the closest thing to a real life simulation. So as an old fart former 90s gamer I know these games are as ancient to young gamers as PacMan was back in my time. Technology has gotten so that no one seems to be bothered by bad game graphics anymore but do I hope this answer sheds some light on the question.

What advice changed your life financially? Observing people’s lives rather than listening to their advice is what inspired my spending habits. So many people who draw some sort of salary have advice about spending that money. Spending advice is at every corner I turn. Here are some examples of such advice I encountered : I get that sort of advice practically everywhere, whether it be my co-workers, acquaintances and within my family, everybody is willing to guide me on how to save a couple bucks here and there with their helpful hints. But one thing that I can never discuss with them is this one taboo question, 'Are you satisfied with the direction of your life?’ Such a question would be considered condescending so such conversation is avoided. I look at the person giving me advice and ask myself does he/she lead the kind of life I want. Do I really want to be that guy stuck in a unfulfilling job to ensure that I pay off my car loan, coming home to an apartment to eat a can of Goya beans every evening? I've met so many people who base their lives around simple analogies: ‘You’re only young once.’ ‘Life is short.’ ‘You can’t eat money.’ ‘Treat yourself.’ ‘Work hard, play hard.’ Regardless of their responsibilities and obligations in life these are their core beliefs and they believe they have the wisdom to offer advice to all listening ears based on their beloved ambiguous three word quotes. In my view this is just a convenient mindset in which one can deny accountability for one self. ‘Honey I'm sorry but I can't pay rent this month. I was hanging out with the boys and one thing leads to another. Life is short. Can you borrow some more money from your parents?’ ‘No I'm not selling my car. This is a limited edition. I'll pay you back what I borrowed before the year is over. Life is short and you can't eat money.’ Sad to say these are the same kind if individuals who are most vocal when it comes to giving advice, personal and financial. If someone's personal lifestyle does not agree with you then do not follow their financial advice. One always goes with the other. In a nutshell I would advise that you stop listening to financial advice from those who place more value on emotional satisfaction. Just my 2¢. A donkey can bray as loud and as often as it feels to but it can never convince anyone that it is a horse.

What show / movie had no right to be as good as it was? Back in 1999 my brother and I was spending some summer vacation time at our cousin's place in Tobago. It wasn't the greatest of vacations because our cousin and her boyfriend were having these vicious fights over money (they weren't in the best place financially and had four daughters below the age of 5). We decided to spend a Saturday afternoon going to the cinema. We didn't care what was on, we just wanted to get away from the endless arguments amidst the chaos of screaming toddlers and mounds of filthy diapers. This was the double feature of the weekend: As a pair of hormone raging, ignorant and slightly sexist teenage boys, you could guess which movie appealed to us more. We were grateful that the 007 movie was showing first so we wouldn't have to stick around to watch Double Jeopardy or as my brother called it The Fugitive….but with a Woman. When The World Was Not Enough ended with its typical 007 sexual innuendo type final scene my brother and I looked at each other and nodded. It was ok. There was a lot of explosions, chase scenes, Denise Richards’ bouncing breasts and shorty shorts but we both knew we were unimpressed. However, in our typical peer influenced macho-vision we pretended that the movie was the real deal. We had the choice of watching Ashley Judd outrun a police car or go home and face adults yelling while half naked toddlers pee themselves in fright. We decided to watch the movie. What a great decisions that was. Double Jeopardy was like a roller coaster ride that got better by the minute. It was far better than The World is Not Enough. It was even better than The Fugitive. When she got her poetic justice in the end my brother and I jumped from our seats and wanted to hug each other in tears. We could give a fart about our macho ideals, Ashley Judd was our sister and she finally been done right. It was that good of a movie! We left the cinema thoroughly satisfied and entertained in so much that the choas that awaited us home didn't seem to matter anymore. I recently rewatched it with the idea that maybe it wasn't that great and maybe because we were dumb teenagers it had made an impression. I was blown away even moreso a thirty something year old dad than as a thirteen year old boy. The movie abandons every cliche there is about on-the-run and fugitive type action thrillers. The lead role is no superhero, there is no stupid forced comic relief character making racist jokes, there is no romantic subplot. Straight up escape and revenge served on a hot plate with Tommy Lee Jones in his best performance ever imho. I sincerely recommend it.

What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"? I worked with a lady in her early 40s at a pizza restaurant. She was just a ordinary grunt like the rest of us. She aspired to be a supervisor but what held her back was that she had 6 kids, three, in their late teens/early adulthood for one father, another two of toddler age for another father and a baby for her recent boyfriend. This domestic situation made it hard for her punctuality and regularity at work as there was always a babysitting issue or child maintenance issue that needed resolving with her two exes. Her current boyfriend was no supportive stalwart himself as practically once every week she would stop her duties to go outside the restaurant to have long and intense arguments with him on the phone in regards to his inability to come pick her up that evening or various other disagreements that they had. In person the boyfriend had a nasty, arrogant attitude and seemed to care only for casual sex, his car and for her to keep his baby away from her older kids whom they all shared a mutual dislike with one another. She lived with her two toddlers and her baby at her father's house which was shared with several other siblings of similar circumstance. With that there was a lot of family fighting in regards to space and ownership. To put it bluntly she lived in a world of shit. Given the circumstances it seemed unlikely that she would be unable break free from the poverty and drudgery any time soon. I would feel the greatest sympathy for her and try my best to help her at work in any regards. That is until that fateful day when I saw her rubbing her stomach and smiling to herself. ‘Looks like you're ready for another one (baby)’ I said jokingly. She smiled and said that she and her current boyfriend (the arrogant dickhead) was trying for another baby. They had a girl and now he wanted a boy. ‘Are you serious?’ I said. I was flabbergasted that she was saying this so casually. It was as if she suddenly reverted back to a naive 16 yr old who found her first love and was no longer a middle aged woman with 6 children and a truckload of problems. One of my biggest flaws is that sometimes I can't keep my opinions to myself. ‘But you have 6 kids already!’ For a second she came out of her dream and reverted back to reality. She glared at me angrily for a split second .Then she returned to her child like persona and replied, ‘Children are a blessing.’ ‘Children are a blessing when you can afford to raise them right and give them the love and attention they need.’ Those words just came out of me in very emphatic tone. As a father of one (I worked part time at the restaurant) I was struggling to survive, working two jobs to ensure that my daughter had a future and to ensure all of my free time was dedicated to her. This lady worked one job and was dependent on family, friends and the Government to assist with any shortcomings she encountered, which seemed to be every day. I could not relate at all to what she was saying. She glared at me again and the conversation ended. An hour later I'm called into the manager's office. Apparently she got so angry she complained to the manager that I was being emotionally abusive, chauvinistic (the restaurant was 90% female staff) and stuck my nose in other people's business. She even told the manager that my words were so hurtful she felt overcome with hurt that she was considering taking a sick day and leaving. I sat and nodded in silence. I was the given a warning and sent out of the office. I learned a sad but valuable lesson that day: Some people are simply destined for a life of hardship and misery through their own stubborn mentality and poor choices. So to answer the question What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"?: People who get offended by the truth.

What are some classic movies with surprisingly conservative themes and agendas? Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory (1971) One of my favourite movies as a child and as an adult I still adore it. However as I've grown older I've noticed, what I believe to be, certain pro conservative aesthetics throughout the movie. Casual acceptance of poverty. In the beginning of the film we observe that Charlie is poor and resides in a one room shack with his mother and four bedridden grandparents. Every day he is given ‘cabbage soup' and though little mention of it is made in the movie, Charlie's father in fact died from a work related incident at a toothpaste factory. Despite this, in no instance does the family complain about their lot in life nor the lack of government assistance. They don't even speak about the toothpaste factory's responsibility towards the father's death. They seem to accept their poverty as no fault of the system but simply bad luck and their current lot in life. The Candyman can… In one scene the owner of a popular candy store serenades a bunch of kids with the now-classic The Candy Man song. We see him liberally tossing various candies and chocolates towards the kids without account or interest in his inventory or cash. One gets the perception that this is some sort of communal children's paradise where all these delightful goodies are given for free by a mystical Candy Man figure only for the camera to pan towards Charlie sadly staring in through the window, out in the cold. We then realize that this is not a child's paradise. The kids are indeed charged for the sweets (and quite possibly the Candyman makes a killing when he sends the bill to the parents). This then reinforces the idea that nothing in this world is free. One thing the Candyman can't do is give free candy. Wonka himself Willy Wonka is portrayed as the quintessential 20th century, eccentric man of wealth and power type persona in the vein of Henry Ford and Thomas Edison. He is extremely private and enshrouds his ‘trade secrets' with fanatical obsession. He is portrayed as friendly, giving and charismatic yet mechanical and indifferent to an almost sociopathic level. Only as I grew older did I notice how much the town looked like a ghetto whilst Wonka himself enjoyed a secret, near magical lifestyle that 99.9% of the population could only dream of. The entire competition was revealed to be simply a ploy to find an innocent and faithful child for Wonka to adopt to continue his legacy. Wonka couldn't care less if the children all died as seen in his reactions to their unfortunate accidents. He hires a man who pretends to be his main competitor to try a staged attempt to find out which of the children were susceptible to bribery. He gets the parents to unwittingly sign contracts to the child's disadvantage without giving them time to read. Who could forget the scene where he yells and berates Charlie and grandpa Joe? This is near the end where they come to claim their lifetime supply of chocolate only to find Wonka fiendishly harping on about their signed contract and ranting about how they voided it by dirtying his ceiling through horseplay. Wonka represents a figure of conservative success at its very worst (or best, according to how you look at it). The Slav…..I mean the Oompa Loompas And of course the controversial Oompa Loompas. Represented as pygmy Africans in the book they are portrayed as singing dwarf like men with flaming orange skin, green hair and silly costumes. So many parodies have been created in regards to the Oompa Loompas actually being a colourful representation of slavery. They aren't allowed outside of the building nor any communication with the outside world and it is negligible if they are given a wage or even enjoy the benefit of basic human rights. The movie posits that Wonka once employed ordinary salaried human workers but had to close the factory for 3 years due to spying and sale of his secret recipes, etc by human employees. If I could dare to be a bit tongue in cheek I'm certain Wonka has a team of armed Oompa Loompa sentries who supervise the others and anyone trying to escape is shot on sight. In conclusion Wonka and his ideals are well suited towards a conservative climate. It is clear that he believes in an hierarchy and that his little world must be governed by a select few of which authority must be transferred to those whom are carefully chosen to be the best to rule and uphold order. He is a staunch capitalist and believes that rules and laws should exist but a few eggs must be broken for progress to continue. On a personal level he is charitable but wary of the majority and he places his own self interest and ambitions above that of the collective problems of the common people of whom he believes create their own problems for themselves whenever given an opportunity. So Willy Wonka is my choice for the greatest movie with hidden conservative themes and agendas, good and bad.

Have you ever witnessed an office prank that cost someone their job? I may be cheating a bit but I can't help to answer such a burning question. I performed a prank that could've cost me my job. In my late teens I worked in a warehouse doing manual labor which mostly included picking up boxes of products, placing them on a trolley and bringing them to the front to be delivered. It could sometimes be rather monotonous especially when the huge orders came in and you spent all day rolling about the massive double warehouse in your creaky trolley that always had one bad wheel. Jason (or J as he preferred to be called) was our supervisor. He was a muscular guy with a deadpan face and shiny bald head. He was the butt of many of our jokes because he spoke in this forced, psudo-sexy whisper and constantly licked his lips while giving his daily inspirational morning speeches (we would call him LL Cool J in secret). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He barely ever smiled and no one saw him laugh, although one of my friends claimed to have seen him laughing at an episode of Rugrats while behind his office computer. Anyways. As I mentioned the job could be monotonous. One evening I saw that one of the older female workers, Erica, had written on the bulletin board. 'I love my fellow workers.’ This irritated me because it was not a bulletin and it had an air of Soviet Communism about it. I wanted to change it to 'I love my fellow COMRADES' and draw a hammer and sickle but I knew that most of my coworkers wouldn't get the joke and it would be ignored. In the end I decided to change it to 'I love my fellow SLAVES.’ That would catch their attention and provide a good laugh and then it would be erased and teach Erica to stop using the bulletin board to write her insipid, brown-nosed statements. Unbeknownst to me J, who was of African descent, was in the process of watching all the episodes of Roots on DVD. He was emotionally charged about African history and slavery in particular. It didn't even occur to me that he was wearing a lot of African themed clothing also. The next morning I arrived just in time for the morning prayer and J's speech. The atmosphere was like a funeral as I entered the warehouse and saw everyone staring at me. J, in a low growl, asked me if I was the one who wrote the slave comment on the board. I replied yes. J licked his lips and made a long, impassioned plea about slavery and black pride. Every time I tried to explain to him that I didn't mean it in a context of race he would say, 'Shut up Jumbo (my nickname).’ He then ended by saying in his low psudo-sexy LL Cool J voice, 'Don't you ever………..ever, ever………let me see you write anything racist on this board again.’ Had I not been of African descent myself I'm certain I would've been put on extended probation, let go or at least spoken to by HR. My friends enjoyed the whole ordeal and it made good scuttlebutt for a few days. I never touched the bulletin board again but being the best impersonator of J, I was sought after by my friends and coworkers to re-enact J's racism speech. I would do a perfect impersonation with exaggerated licking lips and have them howling with laughter. Unfortunately I was called into Js office some time later. I was in trouble. Someone snitched to J that I was mocking how he spoke. I was certain now I would get the boot. Instead I saw J with a big smile on his face watching on his phone a video of me impersonating him. 'Jumbo,' he said and then licked his lips, 'Let me see you talk like me.’ I looked at him and repeated what he just said, licked lips and all. To my surprise he simply smiled and gave a soft 'he he he’ laugh and told me to go back to work and stop fooling around. He did have a sense of humour after all. Myself with some friends at the warehouse. J wasn't present unfortunately.

What type of women should you never date? An acquaintance of an acquaintance of mine was a moderately attractive girl. We all attended the University of the West Indies as Evening students and shared the same course in Management Accounting. I'll refer to her as Sarah. Sarah wasn't the brightest bulb but she had a seemingly friendly disposition and was good with people….well, she was good with just males to be honest. Because she enjoyed a lifestyle of getting into the best parties as a 'promo girl’ (attractive girls dressed in skimpy clothing hired to sell/give away alcoholic beverages) her studies suffered. The night before the final exam she approached me in desperation explaining that she did poorly in her midterm and wasn't ready for this exam. She asked that I come over to her place and we both do an 'all-nighter.’ Being as clever as she was with the opposite sex, she made sure to sumptuously stress on and repeat the word 'all-nighter’ as she was aware it sent erotic images into my mind. Despite originally planning to get some good sleep that night I went over to her apartment. She then served me hot chocolate and cookies whilst moving around in a rather eye popping nightgown. I sat and calmly explained accounting stuff but when 3am reached and I realized that she couldn't get the grasp of the first two chapters, I knew this was going to be a lost cause. I was ready to go home and sleep. However, she rubbed my legs tenderly and gave me puppy dog eyes, explaining how desperate she was to pass this exam. I've always been something of a nice-guy and taking advantage of women in desperation has never been my thing. I asked that she buy lunch after the exam in exchange for staying up all night. We continued and as the wee hours of morning started to break the stillness of the dark, she started getting rather irritable and I condescended to teaching her how to do up legit looking accounting tables and fill them with stuff that's supposed to be there. In my heart I knew she was going to fail. When 8am arrived we were both exhausted. I went home to have a bath and change clothes to ready myself for the exam at 11am. I sat the exam and found it a tad challenging but manageable. However when I glanced back at Sarah her face looked as though she was trying to solve the meaning of life. After the exam ended and everyone filed out the building I headed towards Sarah who bore a disturbed countenance and seemed to be trying to avoid me. I inquired as to her exam experience and she said that it was very difficult and that she didn't even finish half the paper and was certain to fail. I pretended that this wasn't the case. Pondering about the lunch she promised I asked, 'So what's for lunch?’ 'I'm so tired,' she said, 'I need some sleep. See you later.’ She then pulled out her phone as though she just got a phone call and walks the opposite direction from me. Instinctively I know that she is pretending to talk on the phone as a means to get away from me and the topic of her promise to by me lunch. I realize I've been shafted but I tell myself that failing an exam after staying up all night can bring the worst out in anybody. The following semester I'm in the library doing an assignment for marks towards my Statistics midterm. I get a call. I answer it and it's Sarah. I had never even given her my number before. In her typical sugary tones she questions as to how I'm doing and how she doesn't see me around anymore and how I'm so smart she thought I had already finished University with first class honours and yadee yadee yaa. I listen with patience to her insincere flattery knowing fully well that she's looking for some kind of favour. 'Are you doing the Stats course this semester?’ 'Yes,' I stoically replied. I listen as she pretends that this is news to her. She gushes about how it is such a wonderful coincidence and that she is also doing the same course. I already knew this because in the class I had already seen her name signed in the role even though I never witnessed her attending a single class. Clearly she got some naive manchild to sign for her attendance. 'I'm having problems with the stats assignment….you know the one that is due tomorrow. Can I meet you somewhere? I remember how much you helped me for Accounts. I really wish I had a decent, smart guy like you in my life…’ It dawns on me that all the time she really was a deceitful opportunist. I smile as a great idea pops into my head. ‘Are you anywhere near the library?’ 'Yeah,' she replied, 'I'm actually right outside.’ Clearly she had plotted her little scheme very efficiently to the point where she obtained my phone number and location at an instant. 'I'm in the third floor in the carrel in the south west corner.’ I wasn't actually at the south west carrel. However I go to it and take out a folder page. On this I scribble a note and then I fold it and leave on the desk. 'Okay I'm coming now,' Sarah says in an aggressively determined manner. She is so determined she keeps me on the line to ensure that she doesn't lose me to circumstance. 'I gotta leave in a bit,' I tell Sarah. 'You gotta hurry.’ In reality I'm actually gathering my belongings to leave the library. Sarah explains that she has entered 3rd floor while I'm collecting my book bag outside the library. 'I'm at the carrel!’ Sarah tells me with a hint of exasperation as she sees I'm not there.
