What was your cringiest moment with a boss? Ms. B was a former supervisor of mine in a Government building I worked. She was a lady in her early 50’s. She was a nice person but was an eccentric and an introvert to the core. When things were slow she would stay isolated in her office, playing chess online or taking a nap. When she came out of her office her only conversation would usually be short, irritable grumbles about random stuff that annoyed her about the job and the typical ‘can’t wait for the weekend/payday’ talk. Then she would return to her idle privacy. Mary, a co-worker of mine, observing that our supervisor had so much free time on her hands, decided to enroll in an online course. Mary thought it fair she perform her duties during the morning and after lunch work on her online studies. Ms. B began observing this and one day, while stepping out to grab lunch, made a snide comment towards Mary’s direction: ‘Lunch break is just an hour. I don’t want to report people who like to come to work and do their own thing.’ Ms. B’s grumble was directed towards Mary but in a most blunt and condescending manner. Mary, being a woman of passion, could not take such a hypocritical statement without taking some kind of action. For days, she plotted on how she would give Ms. B a piece of her mind; how dare she? Ms. B who does practically nothing, making accusations of others doing as such. They say it’s only thieves who are always paranoid that everyone wants to steal from them. Such and such was the rantings of Mary for that evening. The day Mary decided she was going to confront Ms. B about the statement, something strange happened. Ms. B, in a seemingly good mood, had come out of her office and was helping visitors and getting involved in the day to day operations of junior staff like myself and Mary. Then Mary observed something that made a Cheshire grin spread across her face. ‘Elijah,’ she said, ‘Look at Ms. B’s pants.’ I looked. Ms. B was wearing a beige colored work-pants. Nothing seemed out of the ordinary until I observed that there was a wet, red spot observable from the back, around the crotch area. I stared aghast. Ms. B didn’t seem to notice her period came down on her and clearly had no protection against such an event. She must’ve assumed that her menopause came to an end and periods were now a thing of the past for her. Some of the people she was dealing with seemed to have observed her predicament also but looked as though they felt too awkward to say anything about it. I looked at Mary and said, ‘We should tell her about it.’ ‘No,’ Mary replied, ‘Not right now.’ Mary waited until the very last visitor left the building and the usual evening lull began. Ms. B went into her office and closed the door. I watched as Mary went up to the door, knocked and entered. ~~~~~~~~~~~ Ten minutes later Ms. B, with all her belongings on her, sped past me while uttering, ‘I have to deal with a matter.’ She hastily left the building. Mary told me that when she explained the situation to Ms. B, the look that came upon Ms. B’s face was nothing short of the deepest dread and horror. That for a second she wore the facial expression of a convict at the gallows. I could not help but empathize with the level of cringe Ms. B must've felt on her way back home. Mary got her poetic justice. If she were really mean she could’ve spread the word about the incident through the entire building but the slight torture was enough. Mary and Ms. B began to develop a meaningful relationship after the incident. In other words they started to scratch each other’s back. Maybe it was some sort of neurotic subconscious agreement they both made, as in reminding each other ‘You got me covered right?’ Maybe the situation gave Ms. B a slice of humble pie? I don’t know. What I do know is that to this day I don’t understand women.

What is the most obnoxious type of student for a teacher? I'm not a teacher, but my job requires teaching random subjects to the younger students for a single period a day. In my many years of doing this I've always noticed a trend. Let's pretend this is a class clown. He (let's be honest, most of the time it's a boy) has self esteem issues and believes that the only way his peers can recognize his existence is by drawing attention to himself by disrupting the class with jokes, pranks or just acting as stupid as humanly possible. The class clown is NOT the most obnoxious type of student. These are the students who always laugh at and encourage the class clown, regardless of how unfunny/disruptive his performance. These are the fake audience. They are by far the most obnoxious students in a class. In my experience class clowns tend to go through a phase. Most of them grow out of their clownish behaviours as they get older and many of them actually prove themselves to be thoughtful, intelligent and caring. The fake audience (which usually comprises under 5 students) are the one who are real disruptors of the class. They are the ones who are truly inconsiderate and disrespectful. They usually have a consistently bad attitude. They manipulate the class clown to disrupt the class by providing an audience. This allows for them to channel their defiance and disrespect towards you by using a hapless class clown surrogate. When the giggles have ended and the majority of the class have decided to get serious, the fake audience will urge Mr. Clown to continue his antics. Regardless of how unfunny and irritating the clown's later performance is, they hold their bellies in false laughter in a effort to give rise to anarchy and poor Mr. Clown is held fully responsible and gets in serious trouble. The sad fact is the fake audience, in many cases, do not even like the class clown and have nothing to do with him outside of class. My trick for dealing with class clown disruptions is that I totally ignore him. Instead I concentrate on spotting the fake audience members who are egging him on. I then point them out and bring them to the front of the class, letting them know that they are in trouble for disrupting the class and will be taken to the Principal or Safety Officer's office. Like clockwork this action usually follows. The highlighted fake audience becomes enraged and demonstrate overwhelming disrespect, arguing with me that the class clown is the one who disrupted the class and they are innocent. In a short period of time they reveal themselves for who they are by speaking ill against the clown, they start passionately arguing their rights, some go as far as making threats, some walk out of the class and some point the blame at one another. All in all they reveal themselves to the class (and the class clown) what disrespectful, manipulative, conceited and resentful little creatures they are. Works every time. Edit 5.05.22. Did you ever do something that was insensitive, culturally, racially, or otherwise, and didn't realize it at the time, but do now? I must've been around 6. My cousin P was a 14 year old girl. P used to help my mother with babysitting me when she took my brother and I and ran away from our unstable (at the time) father and home. We were given a temporary lodging at her brother T’s house and P was one of his many children. T was a notorious womanizer and allegedly had many children with various women all around the country. Most of the children he denied paternity and refused outright. Sadly a lot of them grew up homeless or in orphanages. P was one of the three ‘lucky’ ones that T decided to accept paternity and raise. She was always a friendly girl, charming and gifted with an amazing sense of humour. Her voice was almost exactly like Miss Piggy from The Muppets and it was a delight for my brother and I to hear her. However her father was not a role model parent and she grew up missing the majority of school. At 14 she couldn't read or write properly. My mother, through her own sheer ignorance, would go about telling other family members and friends how dunce P was. She didn't notice that I listened to her when she said these things. At one point I heard my mother telling someone that P was so dunce that her 6 year old son (me) knew how to read and write better. As a 6yo, I couldn't decipher right and wrong so seeing that my very own mother openly called P a dunce, I assumed that nothing was wrong with that. The day after when P was babysitting me, she asked me to read one of my story books for her. Full of pride I sat and read it with gusto. After I finished reading P complimented me profusely on my reading skills, asking me if I was the brightest boy in school and whatnot. I then told her something that pains me to this day ‘Mommy says I'm the brightest boy in class. Mommy says you're a dunce. I don't want to be a dunce like you.’ I cannot remember her reaction but I do remember P attempting to laugh it off. What did I do seeing her smiling and laughing the hurt away. I kept repeating that she's a dunce, making a song of it even. P sent me off to play. I'm pretty certain what I said in my naiveté devastated her. P forgave me and my mother in time and no mention was ever made about it. It was only when I grew into my teens did the gravity of the situation finally register. To make matters worse I found out later that P was a victim of sexual abuse from the man she called father at the time. It's something that haunts me to this day when I think of it. Thank God P was a strong person and overcame all those difficulties she faced in life.She still retains that good spirit she's always possessed.

Which boxer’s style do you find the most aesthetically pleasing? Definitely The Lion Lennox Lewis. ‘The Lion’ is such an apt name because he does have a fighting style similar to a large cat. Lennox is a great tactician who uses his left jab to feint, taunt, displace and sometimes to smother and confuse. His left jab is like a diagnostic tool where he feels for the condition of the opponent and when the timing is right he unleashes powerful combinations. When facing shorter opponents he squats in a crab like posture and and uses his long arms and height advantage to monitor his opponents’ status, peering at them like a feline playing with its meal. If his opponent has some fight left in him and attacks, Lewis retreats in his crab like manner, smothering their offense with his own punches or jabbing them into a clinch. However he does not stick to this style. This style works for his shorter, less rangy opponents. When faced with opponents his own size and strength he's can successfully change styles from outboxer/boxer -puncher to brawler/pressure fighter. This is most evident in his fight with Vitali Klitschko where the bigger brawler’s (Klitschko) style was all wrong for Lewis’ clinical style. What I personally find pleasing about Lewis’ style is that you see the punches when they land, you see the frustration in his opponents face and the calmness in his. What I like about Lewis himself is that his boxing comes from a place of emotional maturity and self control. You see his method and you eventually see the results. His style is effective and shows a peek of the sportsmanship that lies in a sport that has its foundation in crude barbarity. Edit: If I could add the fact that Lewis is a seasoned chess player. I don't want to assume that this is a factor contributing to his typically calm and stoic demeanor, his emotional and ring intelligence. If I could dab in his personal life a bit, the fact that he is one of the few boxers to have relative success in his personal/family life, his ability to hang up his gloves and avoid any possible brain damage (as per his wife's plea) the avoidance of drug abuse, party lifestyle, scandal and controversy makes him (to me) an underrated role model in the world of sports on par with the likes of George Foreman. Just my 2¢.

Who was the weirdest kid in your class? Ray was the weirdest boy I ever met in my life. To this day I’ve never come across a boy so profoundly odd as this boy Ray who was a classmate of mine. His story is somewhat of a sad one as he was a slow student from a really poor background. Ray had a learning deficiency and was kept down some grades, making him two years older than the rest of us. He had an early growth spurt and at age 11, he could pass for a stocky and pudgy young man. This made him look absolutely ridiculous in our school uniform. Him squeezing into our generic blue shirt/khaki shorts ensemble and with his socks pulled high upon his leg reminded me of those silly yodeling Bavarian men I would see on TV advertisements. To make it worse. Ray would never stop smiling. He had to his credit an indefatigable attitude towards life. No matter how many insults were thrown his way (by both teachers and students), no matter how often he was bullied or was ignored when football/cricket teams were chosen or was screamed at by his teacher, the principal etc, he would simply smile and laugh away the matter. Ray would’ve made a first rate boxer if he had chosen that direction in life. I saw Ray take several punches in play fights and not a single grimace of pain would appear on his face. During a lunch period several boys made it a game to fling stones to shoo a mangy dog that kept coming near the school for food. Ray who, for some unknown reason, was running around the field by himself ran straight into one of those stones as it collided with his head. He stopped and looked about in a confused manner and then continued running around. No one sat near Ray during class. The teachers endorsed this practice to teach him a lesson to buck up on his schoolwork. Once, I had a falling out with my friends and they told me I was banished from the gang. Angrily, I told them I didn’t care and didn’t need them and went and did the unthinkable. I went and sat next to Ray as the entire class looked on in horror. Ray was absolutely delighted to get a new friend. I feigned interest in being his friend to spite my gang. However, in little time, things started to get weird. I knew Ray was weird but spending the week with him made me realize the extent to his weirdness. Firstly, I accidentally spilt some ink on the desk. I was terrified the teacher would see and I frantically looked for some tissue to wipe the mess. In my amazement I watched as Ray scooped up the ink in his palm and rubbed it into his hair. He smiled and told me that ink gives his hair a good shine. Then we began to discuss our personal lives. I told him the bare basics about my family, as to who it composed of and he immediately began to discuss extremely cringe and taboo subjects about his family such as how he has to help his grandmother wipe her butt after she poos and how he hated when there was a water shortage because his sister had a problem with her, let’s just say ‘personal odors.’ Hearing him speak these things so openly and with a huge smile on his face made me recoil. I decided that conversation was the not the best idea for the two of us. During recess I told Ray that I wanted to be alone for the time being and Ray queried as to why. Ray wanted us two to play ‘Catch’ (Tag) but I explained to him that it would be ridiculous for just two boys to play Catch, that we needed a big group. He then gave me a massive shove that sent me on the ground and started giggling ‘Catch me, catch me.’ He had a very effeminate manner of running and the fact that his pants were way too small and tight made him look atrocious as he giggled and ran around, waiting for me to run after him. My friends saw all this and looked at me with pity and shook their heads in dismay. It all came to an end one morning when my best friend came to me and begged that I return to the gang. I said ‘no way.’ He proceeded to tell me that all the girls and even the teachers were starting to speculate that I was gay and Ray was my boyfriend. With that said I immediately returned to my gang and left Ray in the dust. Sad, but that is how the mindset of an impressionable 9 year old boy can be. I look back in regret at how unintentionally mean I was as a kid and if I were to ever encounter Ray again I would formally apologize for my behavior from decades past. I do hope that he found some measure of success and happiness in his life. But he really was quite a weird kid. Edit 02.02.22 I’ve met several fascinating characters in my youth. Ray was one, this ‘child genius’ named Vachel was another. Click here to read about him.

What was the most disgusting thing you have seen at an auto mechanic shop? This may be cheating a bit but it actually occurred at an auto-electrician's garage. The guys who ran this garage were really nice. And I'm not just saying that as a form of courtesy. They were eerily pleasant to the point that I wondered if they were on some sort of drug or followers of some type of underground Eastern philiosphy/religion. They would never get impatient or irritated with you. There was a calming resonance in their voice that made you feel everything was going to be OK and they would listen to you with the utmost sympathy and understanding. Sometimes I would find myself wanting to visit them even though I had no electrical issues with my vehicle, just to bask in their warmth and friendliness. They were experts at their job too. As one would expect they were quite popular in the area. You would line up for hours to get a spot inside but it was worth it. Absolutely no one who was familiar with them would haggle, speak condescendingly towards or show any form of bad face towards them. That would be like sacrilege. However one guy had to be the one to disrupt the positive energy coming from our beloved hippie electrical-garage commune. In Trinidad we have this phenomenon called ‘wetman.’ A wetman is usually a vain but ignorant young man who thrives on attention. His life revolves around impressing easy women with a show of careless spending, flashy clothes and the official wetman badge of honour, his Nissan Tiida vehicle. For some inexplicable reason this vehicle is coveted by wetmen throughout the country, most likely due to the fact that it is one of the cheapest (foreign used) sedans available. Wetmen are also known to be notoriously cheap, uncouth and many of them live such a flagrantly hedonistic lifestyle, they are forced to secretly live in their Nissan Tiidas. In other words, a wetman is a scoundrel. One faithful day, a wetman joined the queue that we would form by parking outside the garage on a little road alongside the garage. In typical wetman fashion he had his gangsta music blasting at full volume the entire time he was parked. One of the apprentices would habitually pass to check on each person lined up outside to ask what was their problem. Doing this, they would find out who had simple problems that could be fixed at an instant, so he/she could be dealt with immediately and speeden the process. The apprentice went to the wetman who was blasting his music. The wetman only slightly lowered the volume to communicate with the apprentice. The apprentice had to tell the wetman to lower the music some more so he could hear him, which irritated the wetman. ‘My car giving trouble,’ Wetman said, ‘Everytime I switch off I have to ask someone for a jump start to start it back.’ The apprentice pulled out his multimeter and said, ‘Switch off the vehicle and lift the bonnet.’ The wetman scowled and in a venemous tone replied, ‘Brother. Like you not listening to what I saying? Switch off? You expect me to push this car all the way inside your garage?’ I was behind the wetman in the queue I was aghast at how stupid he was. Didn't he realize he was speaking to an actual electrician? Didn't he realize that the apprentice would find a way to get it started again? Wisely, the apprentice decided it was not worth it explaining all that to him and told him to wait until he gets a space inside the garage and the boss would personally deal with his vehicle. Wetman then resumed blasting his music much to the displeasure of myself and the apprentice who was now trying to ask me as to what was the issue I had. The apprentice had to go back over to the wetman and tell him again to lower the volume. ‘What da f**k boy,’ the wetman cried, ‘You all taking so damn long here and I can't listen to my tunes.’ He kept threatening to leave and I was hoping for him to make good on his threat but to my disappointment he remained. A half hour later we are both inside the garage. Realizing that the wetman was trouble, the apprentice wisely went to fetch the boss to deal with him. The boss arrived and Wetman stood outside his vehicle with arms folded. The engine was still running but the bonnet was lifted. Wetman squinted at the engine as though looking for some creature hiding somewhere that was causing his electrical problem. The boss approached and asked him what was the matter. Wetman scowled and replied, ‘I done tell yuh secretary what is the problem. Like you all dumb inside here?’ At that moment everyone's head turned towards Wetman's direction. Someone had blasphemed our precious garage! Everyone waited to see how the boss would handle it. No one ever witnessed any of the electricians lose their cool, especially the boss who was the kindest and most calm of them all. ‘Yes,’ the boss replied without any change of tone ‘Mike told me that you're getting ignition problems. I was just hoping to get some more information so I could know the best way to approach the problem.’ ‘The car not starting,’ Wetman uttered irritatedly, ‘What else you need to know? You is the electrician, not me. A whole hour I waiting outside, I going to lose out on a job I was getting.’ He then did what we Trinis call ‘steups’ which is the noise poorly raised people make to show disgust by sucking spit through your teeth. ‘Switch off the ignition let me run the tester through.’ Again Wetman's face scowled and he got defensive, ‘Brother,’ he growled, ‘I not switching off my engine. Last man I went by make me switch off the engine. He couldn’t fix my problem and I had to push my car out the road and ask someone for a jumpstart. That is failure. You have to fix my problem with the engine running!’ The boss stared at the apprentice and then glanced at the Wetman, who was clearly of a legendary level of stupidity as he stood there defiant and folding his arms. How is the boss going to deal with this one? Everyone was probably thinking the latter question. ‘I understand,’ said the boss calmly, ‘However if we operate on your vehicle while it's running we could destroy your circuits. The danger…’ The boss then paused for second and said, ‘Next Monday is the best day for you to come. We're getting a device that can work on vehicles while the engine is running without damaging anything. It's being shipped from China so give me a call Sunday evening to confirm when you're coming.’ Like magic, the little white lie worked and wetman accepted and left in a hurry to see about his hired job. Everyone breathed a sigh of relief when the ignoramus left. The next time I came, I enquired about the I individual and they happily informed me that someone must've solved Wetman's problem because he never did call or show up again. Or maybe he was offered a starring role in the movie below.

What is the creepiest tree species in the world? Ceiba pentandra or better known in Trinidad and Tobago The Silk Cotton Tree Behold the horror. Local legend has it that a West African witch called Gang-gang Sarah attempted to fly back to her homeland after freedom. She climbed the tallest of these beauties and, in a failed attempt to fly, fell to her death, forever cursing the tree which assimilated her corpse. As can be observed, the tree is very limby and sparse of leaves. Many of these trees, such as the example above, if you squint your eyes it looks like several human figures sprawled about in agonized positions. Legend also has it that it is home to supernatural creatures who reside among it or within its massive trunks. Our grandparents would tell us tales of hearing voices or strange noises when approaching these ominous beings in deep forests. Some would claim encountering douens (lost, unchristened demon-children) Or duppies (malevolent spirits) Or even Papa Bois (Father of the woods) himself whilst within range of these trees in the twilight hour. Besides being unsightly these trees can cause great infrastructural damage to roads and house foundations with their massive roots. In the past, only the most brave soul would dear cut down a silk cotton tree for fear of awaking the wrath of the supernatural. Nowadays, our more modern society sees these trees as giant grotesque headaches that need instant removal. Wouldn’t be surprised if they become endangered in the next 50 years. Sad but true. Why do movies try to make female characters look strong by making male characters look stupid and weak? Hollywood needs to take a course in studying James Cameron. He is without a doubt one of the greatest character writers of the 20th century. This is especially in regards to women. Every female lead he has written has become iconic. They are neither strong nor weak. What they are good at is adapting to their environment/circumstances, using their wits and keeping focus on goals rather than trying to prove how much stronger they are than the opposite sex. Examples include: Ellen Ripley - Aliens Lindsey Brigman - The Abyss Sarah Connor - Terminator/Terminator 2 Helen Tasker - True Lies Rose DeWitt Bukater - Titanic Take a look at all the photos. Tell me what is common among all the women. If you answered fear, uncertainty, anxiety, instability or anything hinting at crippling emotions you are correct. None of these women were stronger or more brave than their male counterparts in these films. However all of them were loyal, intelligent and selfless. They were multifaceted characters, displaying weaknesses in many scenarios and great strength and determination in others. They were all emotional. They all depended on the men around them and in various instances the men depended on them. The relationship between male and female was symbiotic Ellen Ripley offered her experience and intelligence to a group of macho, shoot first, ask questions later, marines to survive an alien invasion. Lindsey Brigman kept the SEAL team from turning into savages, kept the ego of her ex-husband/team leader in check and demonstrated love and humanity to the alien life-forces they encountered. Sarah Connor went from being a relatively weak and mild mannered waitress fighting to survive to an obsessive, violent mercenary and then to a more stable and grounded maternal figure after reuniting with her long lost son. Helen Tasker transformed from a mousy, timid housewife to the world's sexiest woman in a mission to save her marriage, in doing so she saves her husband's life as well and Rose went from being a passive, poor little rich girl to a tragic romantic figure that extended beyond class and wealth. All of these women had their weaknesses. None of them dared to think about defeating/overcoming an obstacle without male help. They were women and they were proud of what they were. Many times they screwed up and many times they made foolish decisions/actions but they always saw the bigger picture. They always knew when it was time to lead and when it was time to serve. They were all globally cherished and were well written female characters. Unlike the ones below.

I got an invitation to a high school reunion where I was bullied. I am successful in my career. I want the satisfaction that I’m doing better than my bullies, but I don’t want to demean myself on that level. Should I go? The fact that you are basing a decision solely on the hurt you felt by underdeveloped humans many years (or decades) ago makes me question the level of your ‘success’ if that is your state of mind. The most successful people I know from high school are the ones who haven't allowed the hurt they've experienced deter them from being decent human beings. They don't let it affect making simple decisions that require just an hour or two of their time, a little small talk here, a little empathy there and would cost less than taking the family to see a movie. This is my class back in '99. If you're trying to spot me I'm the awkward nerd on the far right trying to fit in with the group (I had to invite myself over to the shoot). I had a decent amount of friends but I would honestly say that I didn't really get along with the majority of my classmates. A lot of them were obsessed with MTV lifestyle, being relevant and popular. A lot of them were quite mean to me because I was poor and didn't hide it or attempt to fit into their mould. Also, I had my fair share of encounters with physical and mental bullies. This guy here taking the absolute cake. But I wasn't perfect myself. I could be quite obnoxious, aloof and frivolous and I did act randomly mean to some of my own friends who looked up to me. No child in in the history of high school could be considered a model citizen. High school reunions are not just made up of bullies and assholes. There might also be some of the nice former classmates. Even better, you may meet one or two who were awful back in the day but now matured into caring and sensitive adults. Even better, some of your former bullies might even have the burning desire to apologize to you for all the years of hurt. To go to a high school reunion solely flaunt success to your former bullies reeks of immaturity and borderline narcissism. If the above question is a valid question in your mind then you definitely should not ‘demean yourself’ by going. Just as a final sidenote, I was invited to the above class' high school reunion but chose not to go. Not because of personal dislike but because a special, self appointed committee had formed amongst some the more well-off classmates and they decided to pick and choose who was worthy of being invited to the reunion (my best friends were not invited). No thanks. In a case like that. You definitely ought not to demean yourself by going to such a class reunion.

What was the kindest thing someone did for you when you were young? I was a bit of a scatterbrain as a 10 year old. I used to have after-school lessons that would last until 4pm. One evening, after lessons, I checked my wallet and noticed that my traveling money was missing. Being the bright young lad that I was I calculated that since my home was an hour's drive away, I could walk home and it would only take me 2–3 hours at most. I didn't factor in my calculations that my home was an hour's drive away on the highway. I used to watch a lot of adventure cartoons where the hero treks through forests and vast plains for days on end. I told myself that it would be an adventure just like the cartoons. Fast forward three hours later and I'm only a little after the halfway mark. The sun had long set and I'm about to enter the infamous Cleaver Woods (which was, back then, used by murderers to dump bodies). I'm completely exhausted to the point of laying on the ground crying. Suddenly a tall man in his mid to late 20s calls over to me in a voice in which I immediately sense that belonged to a friendly, humourous type person. 'I was liming (hanging out) with my friends in Curepe and I saw you walking. I went to Arouca and I saw you walking. Now I'm home and I see you're still walking...’ I explained the situation and he began to laugh. 'You're mad,' he said, 'Why didn't you take the bus? It's free for school children.’ I felt like a dope. Indeed I had some bus tickets remaining in my wallet and several buses did pass while I was walking. He went to a shop and returned with a snack and a drink for me. While I ate and drank he told me about the dangers of Cleaver Woods and how I could get killed walking through there at night. He then gave me $10 to get a taxi home. He stayed with me until I was put in a taxi and when I was seated and secured he waved goodbye and left. I was so exhausted I don't believe I even told him thank you or asked his name. He didn't seem to care. It looked like what he just did was something normal for him on a day to day basis. At the time the only thing I thought was nice what he did was how he spent money on me. As I grew older I realized that it was much more than that. He looked out for me. Instead of focusing on his own affairs he narrowed his concentration on me and pondered to my ordeal and my safety and made it his duty to help this random boy who had nothing to do with him. At the time my father was absent from my life. This was my first father figure encounter and I could never forget him and what he did.
